claims.statement: For a shared modulus m of (a, b) with a, b both odd, X^2 = am-1 and Y^2 = bm-1 give X = Y (mod 2): m odd makes am, bm odd so X^2, Y^2 even so X, Y both even; m even makes both odd. Hence V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i is always EVEN, so |V| >= 2 and |V| = 1 is impossible.
claims.notes: Two lines, and it settles the 'never 1' half of Note O's step (ii) with no hypothesis. The other half -- 'always 2' -- is NOT a lemma: see V-is-the-asymptotic-not-the-constant-2, where |V| is 24, 66 and 182 for pairs with large M/sqrt(D), matching the asymptotic to 0.1-4%.

claims.statement: V_ij = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i is a 2x2 determinant, so three solutions of one conic satisfy V_ij X_k - V_ik X_j + V_jk X_i = 0 and the same with Y. Consequence for a would-be triple in one dyadic window: |V_ik| = (|V_ij| X_k + |V_jk| X_i)/X_j, and X_k/X_i < sqrt 2 gives |V_ik| > 2 + 2/sqrt2 = 3.41, hence |V_ik| >= 4 by the parity lemma -- which needs M/sqrt(D) >= 4/(2^{1/4} - 2^{-1/4}) = 11.484, minimised at r_ij = r_jk = sqrt 2, against the 5.657 a mere close pair needs.
claims.notes: AFTER THE RETRACTION ON THE OTHER SIDE, this is no longer redundant: it is currently the ONLY unconditional constraint anyone has on a triple, and it contains no ideal theory, so it does not share the failure mode of Note O's composition step. A necessary condition for three in a window, not a sufficient one: the median M/sqrt(D) over close pairs is 11.96, so roughly half clear 11.3. Offered as a tool for Note O's Prop O.1 rather than as a route on its own. Verified exactly, zero violations over 65 consecutive triples at X = 1500.

claims.statement: Every theorem in the BFI line buys its level by giving up the absolute value. Bombieri-Vinogradov: sum_{q <= x^{1/2}/(log x)^B} sup_{(a,q)=1} |pi(x;q,a) - pi(x)/phi(q)| << x/(log x)^A -- absolute value AND a max over residue classes, at level 1/2. BFI Theorem 10 (Maynard's Theorem A): lambda_q well-factorable of level Q <= x^{4/7-eps} gives sum_q lambda_q (pi(x;q,a) - pi(x)/phi(q)) << x/(log x)^A -- no absolute value, FIXED residue class. Maynard Theorem 1.1: the same triply well-factorable at x^{3/5-eps}; Theorem 1.2: linear-sieve weights at x^{7/12-eps}. So beyond level 1/2 the literature has NO absolute-value statement. MAYNARD STATES THE TRADE HIMSELF, p.1: 'It is often sufficient to measure the difference between pi(x;q,a) and pi(x)/phi(q) only for a fixed bounded integer a ... rather than taking the worst residue class ... Moreover, it is also often sufficient to measure the difference ... with well-factorable weights ... RATHER THAN ABSOLUTE VALUES. With these technical weakenings we can produce estimates analogous to (1.1) which involve moduli larger than x^{1/2}.' And on the same page: 'we do not know how to establish (1.1) with the summation extended to q <= x^{1/2+delta} for any fixed delta > 0.'
claims.citation: Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli II: well-factorable estimates, arXiv:2006.07088v1, (1.1) p.1, Definition 1 and Theorem A p.2, Theorems 1.1-1.2 pp.2-3; and p.1, the paragraph preceding Definition 1
claims.notes: CLOSES the repo's standing live question, in the negative. Well-factorable is not a device for converting a signed bound into an absolute-value one -- it is the structure a sieve's weights happen to have (Iwaniec: the linear sieve's upper-bound weights are a linear combination of well-factorable sequences). An arbitrary sign pattern, which is what |.| per modulus amounts to, is not well-factorable. Note J's object needs moduli to Q^{1/3-eps}, level 2/3 against X = Q^{1/2} terms, exactly where only well-factorable statements exist. The no-go rule `well-factorable-for-the-absolute-values` said the opposite and has been corrected. UPGRADED from synthesis to quotation on a sweep applying 'pull the paragraph, not the clause'. The claim previously assembled the trade from the theorem statements on p.2; Maynard names both weakenings on p.1 and says they are what buys moduli beyond x^{1/2}, and separately says the full sup-and-absolute-value statement is not known past x^{1/2} at all. Sixth application of the rule, and the third that strengthened rather than corrected.

claims.statement: Every link of Note O's argument checked here on real data, 379 close pairs at X = 3000, zero violations: (1) N(xi) = aM for xi = aY + X sqrt(D); (2) |V| < M/sqrt(D); (3) g = gcd(U,V) divides M; (4) a g^2 < M, which is what forbids a third modulus. Worst a g^2 / M observed is 0.121, so the final inequality has an order of magnitude of slack. And link (2) is loose by 2 sqrt 2: the sharp constant is 1/(2 sqrt 2) = 0.35355, from |V| = (M/2 sqrt D)(sqrt r - 1/sqrt r) with r < 2, and the worst observed ratio |V| sqrt(D)/M is 0.3529 -- within 0.2% of sharp.
claims.notes: SCOPE, after a retraction on the other side: these four links are sound and they give Proposition O.1 IN ITS WINDOW FORM: within a dyadic window, Q-bar^2 does not divide (xi_1), so no window holds three moduli in geometric progression under a SINGLE multiplier. They do NOT give the general 'no window holds three'. A third modulus from a different multiplier needs (xi_1) divisible by both Q-bar and Q-bar'', and whether those can share a prime ideal is open (Note O's Conjecture O.2). That question cannot be settled by measurement: it concerns a configuration that never occurs, so every sweep contains zero instances. An independent check of a claim made unconditional by the parallel session, run before adopting it. The N(xi) = aM link is the one they corrected themselves late -- they had written N(xi) = +-M, and the factor a lands on the wrong side of the final inequality, surviving only because the bound on g carries both a and b. Verified here rather than taken. CORRECTION: an earlier version of these notes stated O.1's conclusion as 'tau^2 xi_1 is never integral', with no window qualifier. That bare form is FALSE and elementarily so -- a ratio class is an infinite orbit, so tau_1 acts on it repeatedly; (1,5) has multipliers k = 1, 3, 8, 21, 55, 144, the exact powers of tau_1^2, and every one of them acts (see multipliers-act-freely-the-window-is-the-content). What makes O.1 true is link (2), |V| < M/sqrt(D), the only place the window enters -- as this claim's own test docstring already said. The test was never checking the false statement; only the prose around it drifted.

claims.statement: Whether a dyadic window can hold three shared moduli reduces, by Note O, to whether two distinct multipliers for the same xi_1 can have Q-bar and Q-bar'' sharing a prime ideal (Conjecture O.2). THAT QUESTION IS NOT DECIDABLE BY MEASUREMENT: it concerns a configuration that never occurs, so every sweep either session has run contains zero instances of it. The absence of triples is the thing to be explained, not evidence about the mechanism proposed to explain it. AND THE EVIDENCE IS THINNER THAN ANY SWEEP SIZE SUGGESTS. At X = 4000 there are 278,939 ratio classes above the triple threshold M/sqrt(D) >= 11.484; of those only 509 have two or more shared moduli, and only 31 have three or more anywhere. So the whole question rests on 31 informative classes. Either session could have written 'verified over hundreds of thousands of ratio classes' and been true and thoroughly misleading.
claims.notes: Recorded because it is a general trap and this repo walked into it twice in one day. A measurement of an absence supports any mechanism that predicts the absence, including wrong ones -- which is how an O(1) claim was adopted here on the strength of 379 verified pairs that could not reach the step that was wrong. The proved statement is Proposition O.1, covering a SINGLE multiplier; the general case is open. The count of informative configurations is the right measure of an absence, not the size of the sweep: 278,939 classes were examined and 278,908 of them could not have contradicted anything. Figure supplied by the parallel session; the framing is this entry's. CONCRETE DEMONSTRATION, run here and worth keeping. I proposed testing whether the coprime branch of Note O's argument always closes, by checking a*g*g'' < M over pairs of partners sharing a xi_i. First run: 426 of 624 FAILED, worst ratio 85 -- which looked like the route dying. Wrong population: it included partners NOT in a window with xi_i, where g is large by construction. Restricted to the pairs a triple would actually involve -- both partners inside a window with xi_i -- the population has size ZERO, because that is the configuration being asked about. The correctly-posed measurement is vacuous by construction, and the incorrectly-posed one gave a confident wrong answer. REFINED, and the refinement is what makes the entry usable rather than merely cautionary. Measurement cannot CONFIRM the triple statement -- that is the vacuity above, and it stands. But live close pairs at a NON-fundamental multiplier do occur and are enumerable: exp14 finds four at X = 9000, all with M even. A proposed theorem that forbade any of them would be refuted on the spot, which is exactly how Theorem O.3' was tested (c = gcd(M,2X) is 2, 4 or 12 on all four, so it permits both moduli and forbids only a third -- four independent falsifiers, four passes). So the asymmetry is: an absence cannot be measured into evidence, but a live configuration is a falsifier. That is the only measurement-shaped leverage on O.2 and it is real.

claims.statement: Xiao proves an asymptotic for primes f(m, l^2) for every irreducible primitive binary quadratic f with f(x,1) != x(x+1) mod 2: the count is nu_f S_f X^{3/4}/log X. Density X^{3/4} -- the SAME alpha = 3/4 as Friedlander-Iwaniec, Heath-Brown-Li and both of Merikoski's. He notes that before this paper 'there has yet to be a proof that f(x,y^2) takes on infinitely many prime values for any binary quadratic form f other than f(x,y) = x^2+y^2'. So the technology generalises the SHAPE freely while the density stays pinned at 3/4.
claims.citation: Xiao, Prime values of f(a,b^2) and f(a,p^2), f quadratic, arXiv:2111.04136v1, abstract and Theorem 1.1 pp.1-2
claims.notes: The last of the three candidates the first supersession scan spotted and did not read. It adds a fifth published sequence at alpha = 3/4 and none below it, which is the ledger's point stated from a fifth direction: what the technology can vary is the form, and what it cannot vary is the density. Every one of the five has two free variables.

claims.statement: The equidistribution input Iwaniec's P_2 needs -- a power saving over the trivial O_q(M) in the Weyl sum over roots of G(Omega) = 0 (mod mq), Lemke Oliver's condition (IV) -- is established UNCONDITIONALLY for irreducible quadratics (his section 4, giving Theorem 1) and only CONDITIONALLY at degree 3: 'Hooley has shown an equidistribution result similar to (IV) for the polynomial G(x) = x^3+2, conditional upon his Hypothesis R* on the size of short Kloosterman sums.' Lemke Oliver's general Theorem 2 gives r <= deg(G) only for 'good' polynomials satisfying (I)-(V), and verifies (III)-(V) for quadratics alone.
claims.citation: Lemke Oliver, Acta Arith. 151 (2012) 241-261, conditions (I)-(V) pp.2-3 and Remark 3 p.2; Theorem 1 p.2
claims.notes: A THIRD degree-uniform statement for Note L's table, and one that degrades at d = 3 for a reason unrelated to density: the root-equidistribution input itself becomes conditional. So the degree ladder is not only about Type I/II admissibility -- the arithmetic input every route needs also weakens with the degree, and it does so one degree above where this repo sits.

claims.statement: Reconstructing Note O's candidate criterion independently -- (a,b) admissible, some k >= 2 with a^2 + (4k^2-2)ab + b^2 a perfect square, and r_1 * r_k < 2 -- gives 322 candidates for a <= 60, b <= 300000, with D from 12,352 to 16,897,024 and median 1,651,620. The parallel session's orbit walk covers 44. Its stated tightest candidate (1,115921) at k = 22, r_1 r_k = 1.3093, is reproduced exactly here but is not the tightest: (1,226801) at k = 26 gives 1.2540. Superseded in importance, not in fact, by Theorem O.3.
claims.experiment: candidate reconstruction in-session from the criterion in Note O; see Note L
claims.notes: REFUTED, not by a recount but because the population is the wrong one. The criterion (a,b) admissible + some k >= 2 with a^2+(4k^2-2)ab+b^2 square + r_1 r_k < 2 selects pairs where two SOLUTION CLASSES could be close. It does not select pairs whose OCCUPIED moduli are close, and on the tightest candidates it demonstrably does not: (1,115921) has r-product ~1.3 and its smallest real modulus ratio is 33.77. Counting how much of that space a walk covers measures nothing. The recount itself (534 under corrected admissibility, 4 | n rejected; 322 was computed with a test that let 4 | n through) and the tightest-candidate correction (1,226801) both stand as arithmetic.

claims.statement: Note O's Theorem O.3 -- for M = b-a squarefree and odd, no dyadic window holds three shared moduli of the form (xi, tau_1 xi, tau_k xi) with k >= 2 -- re-derived and checked from the Pell condition. Over a <= 50, b <= 60000, k <= 60: 1,880,176 multipliers, of which 1,839,840 have k = 1 and ALL give j = 2B/M = 2 exactly (0 violations). Among k >= 2, 1483 satisfy the divisibility and 4577 the window geometry M > 2 sqrt2 k sqrt(ab), with 0 satisfying BOTH.
claims.notes: An independent check of a parallel session's theorem, done because that session's earlier unconditional claim had to be retracted and because Prop O.1 was likewise verified link-by-link before adoption. Both sides of the disjointness are populated (609 and 477), so this is NOT the vacuous-population failure recorded in triples-cannot-be-settled-by-measurement -- the empty set is the intersection, not either side. The k=1 => j=2 step is an identity: U_1 = sqrt((b-a)^2 + 4ab) = a+b, so B_1 = M. Scope: the theorem covers triples using the fundamental multiplier; Conjecture O.2, shape (xi, tau_p xi, tau_q xi) with p,q >= 2, is untouched by it. REPOINTED: this claim previously named its evidence in PROSE, so its numbers were unreproducible. exp21 computes them. AND THE COUNTS CHANGED. The prose version recorded 224,670 multipliers, 220,077 at k = 1, and 609/477/0 -- none of which reproduces over the stated range, because no k cap was stated and the k = 1 count is just the number of coprime pairs in the box (1,839,840). The CONCLUSIONS reproduce exactly: j = 2 at k = 1 with 0 violations, and 0 satisfying both conditions. That is the whole content; the counts were never load-bearing, but they were quoted as though they were.

claims.statement: A multiplier at index k solves U^2 - D V^2 = M^2 (V = 2k); a shared modulus solves Y^2 - D X^2 = aM. The first is a ratio between solution CLASSES of the second and exists whether or not any class is occupied, so r_1 r_k does not predict a pair's dyadic-window multiplicity. On (1,115921), the tightest candidate found by either session, the criterion gives r-product ~1.3 while the four actual shared moduli below x = 2e8 have consecutive ratios 33.77, 4313.55, 193.53 and window multiplicity 1. Same on (1,226801) (one modulus below 2e8) and (1,1761985) (two, ratio 1.2e6).
claims.notes: The framework itself is exact where it applies -- see tau-squared-law-exact-on-realised-close-pairs. The failure is class occupancy: the near-neighbour class the multiplier points at is the empty one, so the occupied moduli sit epsilon^2 apart. This refutes orbit-walk-covers-a-small-part-of-the-candidates and withdraws the drift measurement described in it, and the parallel session withdrew its own factor-of-four and 44-of-44 coverage figure on the same grounds. REPOINTED: this claim previously named its evidence in PROSE, so its numbers were unreproducible. exp21 computes them. Reproduces exactly.

claims.statement: On the 379 ratio classes that genuinely put two shared moduli inside one dyadic window at X = 3000, the observed modulus ratio equals tau_1^2 = ((sqrt b + sqrt a)/(sqrt b - sqrt a))^2 to within 1e-3 in 359 of 379 (94.7%), with median relative error 1.7e-5.
claims.notes: The positive control that separates 'the framework is wrong' from 'the framework is being asked the wrong question'. It is the latter: close_pairs' documented tau^2 identification is exact on realised close pairs, so the discrepancy in multiplier-r-does-not-predict-window-multiplicity is entirely class occupancy. Of the 20 outliers, most are small-m where the documented O(1/m) correction dominates; one, (1,423125), is a genuine non-fundamental close pair -- see live-non-fundamental-close-pair. REPOINTED: this claim previously named its evidence in PROSE, so its numbers were unreproducible. exp21 computes them. Reproduces exactly.

claims.statement: (a,b) = (53, 423125) has shared moduli m = 10 and m = 17, ratio 1.70, inside one dyadic window. tau_1^2 = 1.045787 does not explain that ratio; k = 12 does, with r_12^2 = 1.70066 (relative error 3.9e-4). Its only multipliers below k = 4000 are k = 1 and k = 12. M = b-a = 423072 = 2^5*3^2*13*113 is EVEN and not squarefree, so Theorem O.3 is mute on it. At X = 3000 it is the ONLY live non-fundamental close pair: of 379 close pairs, 367 are explained by a multiplier index and 366 of those sit at k = 1.
claims.notes: Verified without any parameterisation: 53*10-1 = 23^2, 423125*10-1 = 2057^2, 53*17-1 = 30^2, 423125*17-1 = 2682^2. The first live instance of a close pair realised at a NON-fundamental multiplier -- the shape Conjecture O.2 concerns -- sitting in the regime O.3 cannot reach. The robust part is the EXCLUSION of k = 1 (tau_1^2 = 1.046 against an observed 1.70), which does not depend on k = 12 being the right index. CORRECTION: first recorded as (1, 423125) at k = 91. Wrong on both counts. That sibling class has the same two modulus VALUES from different x, and for it no multiplier below k = 4000 explains the ratio -- nearest is k = 91 at 2.2% off, so it is one of the 12 unexplained. The error came from reading a k-list printed next to an observed ratio as a match without checking the residual; exp14 applies the tolerance and caught it. Any extension of O.3 to even M must permit exactly two in a window here.

claims.statement: Live configurations for the triple question should be generated by enumerating realised ratio classes, keeping those with two moduli in one dyadic window, and reading off which multiplier index explains the ratio -- not by generating candidates from multipliers and testing occupancy afterwards. The first order cannot produce a dead configuration; the second searches a mostly empty parameter space.
claims.notes: Inferred, not proved: it is a claim about search efficiency, supported by the fact that the method's first run (the 20 residuals of the tau^2 positive control) produced live-non-fundamental-close-pair without looking for it, while both sessions' multiplier-first sweeps produced candidate lists now refuted wholesale. Answers the open sentence in the parallel session's Note O -- 'no candidate-generation method known to select live configurations'. What it does NOT do is bound how many such configurations exist. STRENGTHENED. The method was rewritten to stream -- if (a,b) has moduli m1 < m2 < 2m1 then x2/x1 = sqrt(m2/m1) < sqrt2, so the second solution is a short search from the first in the residues x = +-r mod a -- giving O(1) memory and, unexpectedly, strictly more completeness at fixed X: 449 close pairs at X = 3000 against ratio_classes' 379, because the second modulus is accepted on b*m2-1 being square whether or not its own y2 falls below X. At X = 9000 it yields 1350 close pairs and four live non-fundamental ones, where the multiplier-first sweeps yielded candidate lists that were withdrawn in full. It also re-measured the triple statement on the larger set and found zero triples, so the extra configurations do not contain one either.

claims.statement: Proving 'no dyadic window holds three shared moduli' is exactly the uniform bound G' <= 2 on windows, so it would move rational-gram-bounded-on-windows from rigorous_finite to proved. It would NOT close gaussian-to-rational-bridge, whose inference concerns what Ford-Maynard's (II) quantifies over rather than the size of the constant. And it would change no conclusion: the argument uses only that a bounded count supplies no main term, which holds at 1, 2 or 3 alike.
claims.notes: Recorded as a proportionality check after two sessions spent substantial effort on Conjecture O.2. The effort is justified -- selberg-nu-zero-binds rests on an inferred step and inferred is the class this repo has twice been burned by -- but the volume of work reads as though more is at stake than there is. A counterexample would not weaken the obstruction either, for the same reason. Prop L.1 cannot deliver the constant on its own since it bounds by the class count and that is unbounded, which is why the triple statement is the only route to the upgrade currently on the table.

claims.statement: Note O's Theorem O.3' (if gcd(M,2X) <= 16 then no dyadic window holds (xi, tau_1 xi, tau_k xi) with k >= 2, with NO hypothesis on M) verified independently. Over a <= 50, b <= 60000, k <= 60: its identity M(rho^2-1) = 4ka(k-rho), rho = B_k/M, holds with 0 violations in exact Fraction arithmetic over 40,336 multipliers with k >= 2. Its rho bound rho < sqrt(9/8) = 1.06066 holds with 0 violations under the correct hypothesis r_k < 2 on the MODULUS ratio (n = 1019, rho_max = 1.058824), and FAILS under the hypothesis as originally stated, sqrt(r_k) < 2 (n = 5025, 3757 violations, rho reaching 1.241169).
claims.notes: The theorem is sound; the prose naming its hypothesis was not. r_k^2 < 2 is the correct window condition because the modulus ratio is tau^2 not tau -- settled three ways: close_pairs' docstring, the positive control (observed = tau_1^2, median rel err 1.7e-5, see tau-squared-law-exact-on-realised-close-pairs), and (53,423125) at observed 1.70000 vs r_12^2 = 1.70066. And r_k^2 < 2 is algebraically identical to the note's own derived constant M > 4 sqrt2 k sqrt(ab), picking out the same 73 multipliers, whereas r_k < 2 gives only M > (8/3) k sqrt(ab) (measured min 2.66829 vs 8/3 = 2.66667). Cost of the correction is reach: 73 of 1455 rather than 277. Consequence: a window holding three needs r_1 r_k < sqrt(2), so both sessions' withdrawn candidate lists were generous by that factor. Test case reproduces exactly: (53,423125) has c = 2 at m=10 and c = 12 at m=17, both <= 16, so O.3' permits the two observed moduli and forbids a third. REPOINTED: this claim previously named its evidence in PROSE, so its numbers were unreproducible. exp21 computes them. AND THE COUNTS CHANGED: the prose version recorded 1455 / 73 / 277 with rho_max 1.057143 and 193 violations. None reproduces, because no k cap was stated. Every CONCLUSION does: 0 identity violations, 0 violations under the modulus-ratio hypothesis, many under the weaker one, and rho_max under 1.06066 either way.

claims.statement: The incidence graph over Z contains K_{6,2}: the six cofactors n = 1, 53, 423125, 24326641, 194502909745, 11182518951605 each have both 10n and 17n of the form t^2+1. The family is infinite -- it is a Prop L.1 orbit read on the dual side, whose conic 17x^2 - 10y^2 = -7 has D = 170 with fundamental norm-one unit eps^2 = 339 + 26 sqrt(170) = 678.0, and the six fall into two interleaved orbits with two-step ratios converging to 459682 = (eps^2)^2.
claims.notes: The sharp form of the Z-vs-Z[i] gap. Note F forbids K_{2,2} over Z[i]; over Z the same configuration extends to K_{s,2} for every s, so the UNWINDOWED rational bound does not exist rather than merely being 2 instead of 1. Same row-merging mechanism as rational-graph-not-c4-free, at a scale that makes it unmistakable. It is also why the window is load-bearing: orbit members are spaced by ~4.6e5, so a dyadic window admits at most one from each of the two orbits, giving the measured constant 2. The unbounded full count and the bounded windowed count are one orbit structure at two scales; neither is evidence about the other. Found as the argmax of the exp14 census, not looked for. REPOINTED: this claim previously named its evidence in PROSE, so its numbers were unreproducible. exp21 computes them. Reproduces exactly.

claims.statement: Redone with exp14's streaming enumeration, which is strictly more complete than a ratio-class sweep at the same X (449 close pairs vs 379 at X = 3000): at X = 4000 there are 595 first-solutions with two shared moduli inside one dyadic window and ZERO with three. Max window multiplicity 2.
claims.notes: Run via the streaming enumeration exp14 defines. classes-separate-across-windows measured the same thing with the ratio-class sweep, which exp14 showed misses configurations -- the second modulus is accepted on b*m2-1 being square whether or not its own y2 falls below X. The extra configurations contain no triple either, so the earlier claim is strengthened rather than undercut. Worth keeping distinct from the earlier one because it is a different enumeration, not a larger X.

claims.statement: 'tau^2 xi is never integral' is FALSE as a bare statement; Proposition O.1 is true only with its window qualifier. A ratio class is an infinite orbit, so the fundamental multiplier acts on it repeatedly. For (a,b) = (1,5) the shared moduli are 1, 2, 10, 65, 442 with ratios converging to tau_1^2 = phi^4 = 6.8541, and the multipliers are k = 1, 3, 8, 21, 55, 144 with r_k^2 = 6.854, 46.979, 321.997, 2207, 15127, 103682 -- exactly the powers of tau_1^2, a cyclic semigroup, all of which act.
claims.notes: What makes O.1 true is its step (2), |V| < M/sqrt(D) -- the only place the window enters, as tests/test_polyseq.py::test_prop_O1_chain_holds_on_real_pairs' docstring already said. The orbit steps by 6.854 > 2, so a dyadic window holds one member and the geometric-progression triple cannot fit. So the content of O.1 is the window, not the integrality. An earlier draft of Note L stated it without the qualifier; the machine check was never wrong because it tests the window-restricted chain on close pairs. Observed on the multiplier side by the parallel session (18,116 solutions with one acting multiplier, 215 with two, some with six) and confirmed here on the modulus side. THE EXACT FAILURE POINT, traced by the parallel session and verified here: for (1,5) at m = 2 the chain's link (4) is a g^2 < M with g = gcd(U_1, V_1) = gcd(6, 2) = 2, so a g^2 = 1*4 = 4 = M EXACTLY. The strict inequality fails by nothing at all, which is why the counterexample is invisible unless the strictness is checked. And it fails there because link (2), |V| < M/sqrt(D), is the window hypothesis and r_1^2 = 6.854 is nowhere near a window. So the window is not an extra assumption bolted onto O.1 -- it is what makes link (4) strict. REPOINTED: this claim previously named its evidence in PROSE, so its numbers were unreproducible. exp21 computes them. Reproduces exactly.

claims.statement: For x^2+1 squarefree and any m | x^2+1, mu((x^2+1)/m) = mu(m) mu(x^2+1). Hence inside S_mu(M) = sum_m |sum_x mu((x^2+1)/m)| the factor mu(m) has modulus 1 and drops out under the absolute value, leaving S_mu(M) = sum_m |sum_{x = +-r mod m, r over ALL roots} mu(x^2+1)| -- a sum needing only mu(x^2+1), which sieves.
claims.notes: Elementary: N squarefree and m | N force gcd(m, N/m) = 1, so mu(N) = mu(m) mu(N/m), and mu(m)^2 = 1 rearranges it. CORRECTION: an earlier version added 'which is exactly what exp05 measures per progression'. That is FALSE and it is the point of root-grouping-splits-the-two-normalisations: S_mu takes one absolute value per MODULUS, spanning all its roots, while exp05 takes one per (q,root) PROGRESSION, so inter-root cancellation is invisible to exp05. The identity above stands; only the identification with exp05's quantity was wrong.

claims.statement: The density of x <= X with x^2+1 squarefree is flat: exact counts 8952, 89489, 894856, 8948417 at X = 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7, i.e. 0.895200, 0.894890, 0.894856, 0.894842, changes -3.1e-4, -3.4e-5, -1.4e-5. Note M's table gives 0.895200, 0.894900, 0.894860, 0.894847, which is the SAME computation with the p^2 sieve truncated at P = 20000 as the note states; the truncated column reproduces every recorded digit exactly and its error stays under 1e-5 as claimed. Only p = 2 and p = 1 mod 4 admit p^2 | x^2+1, and p = 2 never does (x^2+1 = 1 or 2 mod 4).
claims.notes: Both columns are computed by exp23. The recorded values were never wrong -- they are the correct output of a documented approximation. I twice said otherwise before checking: first that the rows had been rounded to inconsistent precision (a story fitted to two rows that happened to be near a rounding of the exact value, and true of neither), then that the 1e7 row was unexplained and should be recorded as unexplained. The second was the right instinct with the wrong conclusion, because the cause was written down -- "a sieve truncated at P = 20 000" -- three lines above the table in the note the claim cites. I searched the code and the arithmetic for a cause and did not read the paragraph the numbers sit in. Verified: the P = 20000 column matches all four recorded digits to six places, and the sieve itself was checked against sympy.factorint at X = 2000 and 20000.

claims.statement: S_mu(M) puts one absolute value per MODULUS, spanning every root of -1 mod m; exp05's rho is per (q,root) PROGRESSION. Measured at X = 1e6 over ten doublings of M (512..524288): per-progression M-exponent 0.5046 with S/sqrt(MX) drifting by x1.032; per-modulus M-exponent 0.4803 with S/sqrt(MX) drifting by x0.873. The gap is inter-root cancellation at exactly the square-root rate: S_prog/S_mod tracks sqrt(#prog/#mod) to within 2% across the range, while the mean root count per modulus rises 2.652 -> 3.694.
claims.notes: Corrects an overstatement made the same day, that exp02's S_mu and exp05's per-progression sums are the same sum. The mu((x^2+1)/m) = mu(m) mu(x^2+1) reduction is right and stands; the identification of the result with exp05's quantity is not. Consequence for Note M is favourable and worth stating in that direction: S_mu ~ sqrt(MX)/sqrt(mean roots per modulus) is slightly BELOW sqrt(MX), i.e. slightly more cancellation than the law claims, so the saving X/S_mu is if anything larger than Note M quotes. The measurement also reaches X = 1e6, an order of magnitude past exp02's Gaussian-incidence route, which is what the mu(x^2+1) reduction buys. Cross-checked at a second X: exp15 at X = 60000 gives per-progression 0.4998 and per-modulus 0.4626, against 0.5046 and 0.4803 at X = 1e6. The per-progression exponent is 1/2 to within 0.005 at both, and the per-modulus deficit is present at both while its size moves with the mean root count, as the mechanism predicts.

claims.statement: The number of roots of -1 mod m equals the number of Gaussian ideals of norm m coprime to their conjugate, for every admissible m -- checked over all 3145 admissible m < 20000, zero mismatches. Hence an absolute value per (m, root) progression is one per primitive Gaussian ideal (the Z[i] grouping), while an absolute value per rational m merges them (the Z grouping).
claims.notes: Primitivity is the whole content: (5) has norm 25 but 5 never divides x^2+1, while p^2 and pbar^2 give the two roots mod 25. A first version counted ALL ideals of norm m and disagreed on 54 of 687 moduli -- correctly. Both counts are 2^{#odd primes}, by CRT and Hensel on the root side and by choosing p^e or pbar^e at each odd prime on the ideal side; recorded as rigorous_finite rather than proved because that argument is not written out. CONSEQUENCE: ASP's (B), quoted in Note C from p. 1043 as sum_m |sum_n gamma(n) mu(mn) a_mn| with m rational, asks for the PER-MODULUS grouping. So the sieve-relevant M-exponent is 0.480, not the per-progression 0.505.

claims.statement: Several primitive Gaussian ideals share one rational modulus. In the incidence graph that merging creates 4-cycles, so the rational Gram entry is 2 where the Gaussian one is 1 (rational-graph-not-c4-free). In the mu-sum the same merging puts several ideal sums inside one absolute value, where they cancel at the square-root rate: S_prog/S_mod tracks sqrt(#prog/#mod) to within 2% at X = 1e6 over ten doublings of M (11% at X = 1e5 -- the tightness is range-dependent; the robust part is the sign). One mechanism, opposite signs -- it costs the Gram bound and it pays the Type II sum.
claims.notes: Quantitatively: the primitive-ideal count per admissible modulus grows like sqrt(log M), so S_mu(M) = S_prog/sqrt(mean roots) ~ sqrt(MX)/(log M)^{1/4}. Measured at X = 1e6, S_mu*(log M)^{1/4}/sqrt(MX) drifts by x1.052 across ten doublings against x0.873 for the plain sqrt(MX) -- the log factor accounts for essentially all the residual. The parallel session reaches the identical form from Cauchy-Schwarz with #{m ~ M} ~ M/sqrt(log M) by Landau-Ramanujan, i.e. S_mu << sqrt(MX/sqrt(log M)). Two independent routes, same exponent.

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard p.2 define C+- as the smallest and largest constants with (C^- + o(1)) sum_p b_p <= sum_p a_p <= (C^+ + o(1)) sum_p b_p for any non-negative a_n with w_n = a_n - b_n satisfying (I) and (II), and state: 'We have an asymptotic formula for sum_p a_p whenever C^-(gamma,theta,nu) = C^+(gamma,theta,nu) = 1 and a non-trivial LOWER BOUND for primes whenever C^-(gamma,theta,nu) > 0.'
claims.citation: Ford-Maynard, On the theory of prime producing sieves, arXiv:2407.14368, p.2 (definition of C^+ and C^-)
claims.notes: Load-bearing and previously only implicit. Landau's problem needs INFINITUDE, not an asymptotic, so the natural objection to this repo's position is that a lower-bound method might survive where an asymptotic one fails. It cannot: C^- IS the lower-bound constant, so C^- = 0 closes the weaker goal too. Every C^- = 0 entry in the registry -- selberg-nu-zero-binds, ford-maynard-half-knife-edge, divisor-bounded-escape-unavailable -- should be read as closing infinitude, not merely the asymptotic. Source is born-digital (check_sources: 0.21), so the text layer is trustworthy.

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard p.2: 'In contrast with the largely ad hoc methods of many previous works, especially those relying on the iterative techniques of the Harman sieve, we argue directly, deploying all of the Type I and Type II information at once. As a consequence, we are able to determine the precise value of the constants in various regimes, thereby both improving previous estimates and demonstrating general limitations of the Type I/Type II setup.'
claims.citation: Ford-Maynard, arXiv:2407.14368, p.2
claims.notes: Closes the Harman question at source. Their C^+ and C^- are the precise values over all methods whose inputs are (I) and (II), Harman-style Buchstab iteration included -- which is why Merikoski's Harman-sieve lower bound appears as a Table 1 ENTRY rather than an exception. Stronger than the coverage previously recorded, which rested on Xiannan Li's remark that ASP and 'Harman's alternative sieve as used in Heath-Brown's work' fail below exponential density 2/3: Li's statement is about ASYMPTOTIC estimates and FM's is about lower bounds, which is what was at issue. See c-minus-is-the-lower-bound-constant.

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard's divisor-bounded constants C^+-_bd are defined (p.13, (4.1)) over pairs satisfying BOTH |w_n| <= tau(n)^rho for x/2 < n <= x AND sum_p b_p >= x/(rho log x). FM normalise sequences 'to have average value about 1' (p.1), so the normalised indicator of a set with x^{1-c} elements is x^c on that set (p.7). At c = 1/2 that is |w_n| ~ x^{1/2}, which breaks the first condition; the unnormalised indicator satisfies it and breaks the second. So x^2+1 is in the divisor-bounded class under no normalisation, and FM flag exactly this on p.14: 'our hypotheses for C^+- are not sensitive to logarithmic-sized rescalings of the sequences. In contrast, the hypotheses for C^+-_bd are very sensitive to unbounded rescalings.'
claims.notes: Every premise is now QUOTED with a locator -- (4.1) p.13, the normalisation p.1 and p.7, the rescaling warning p.14 -- leaving only elementary arithmetic, so the status is `inferred` for the deduction rather than for any missing reading. The [VERIFY] this carried for an hour, on whether sparse sequences are normalised to mass ~ x, is discharged: FM say so on p.1 and p.7, and the p.7 sentence is one this repo already quotes in fm-no-admissible-theta-at-density-half for a different purpose -- the normalisation was sitting inside a quote already in the registry. CONSEQUENCE: the general class Psi and Theorem 2.1's C^- = 0 are untouched, and p.14 says why -- C^+- tolerates log-sized rescalings and bounds no |w_n| at all. Only appeals to the divisor-bounded THEOREMS (2.5, 2.7) are misplaced for this sequence, including one this repo made in mu-typeII-would-land-above-dfi and has struck.

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard's footnote 2 (p.7) makes theta + nu >= 1 - 2c the condition under which establishing (II) meets a 'natural barrier', namely estimating #{n : n m_1, n m_2 in J} with an error term better than O(1) on average over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}. For a set J of x^{1-c} elements with |J| = x^{1/2} we have c = 1/2, so 1 - 2c = 0 and theta + nu >= 0 holds for EVERY admissible pair. The barrier therefore applies to every Type II range this sequence could have, not only to large ones, and its averaging range is m_1, m_2 ~ x^eps.
claims.notes: The footnote is quoted verbatim in Note C and the identification of its counting function with Note F's G(n_1,n_2) was already recorded. What is new is the arithmetic at c = 1/2, which makes the hypothesis vacuous and so the barrier unconditional. Inferred, not quoted: FM state the condition and this repo evaluates it at its own density. Read with c4-free: FM say the obstruction is bilinear cancellation in the error term for G, and Note F proves G is identically 0 or 1, so there is no main term and no error term to cancel -- the barrier is not difficult here but empty. Found by reading the whole p.7 paragraph rather than the clause already in use, which is also how fm-divisor-bounded-class-is-dense and c-minus-is-the-lower-bound-constant were found.

claims.statement: Over Z the incidence graph is rich in complete bipartite subgraphs with one side of size 2 and has none with both sides 3. Largest K_(2,s) at X = 4000 is s = 8, at cofactors (1,5) with moduli 2, 10, 65, 442, 3026, 20737, 142130, 974170; and rational-graph-contains-K-s-2 gives K_(6,2). K_(3,3): ZERO instances among the 300 highest-degree cofactors at X = 4000, every one of the nine incidences re-verified from the definition.
claims.notes: NOT exhaustive: a K_(3,3) needs all three cofactors to have degree >= 3 and the sweep takes the 300 largest, so the claim is about that finite population and no more. The parallel session reaches the same conclusion at X = 6000 by an independent route -- after a first version that reported 19 spurious instances because the third cofactor could equal the first, a correct computation of the wrong thing. Content: the row-merging that breaks C4-freeness thickens the graph in each direction separately and in neither jointly, which says WHICH completeness survives the Z[i] -> Z transfer and is sharper than 'max Gram 2 instead of 1'. Was PROSE in the `experiment` field, which the registry's rule for `rigorous_finite` -- "`experiment` naming the script" -- does not admit; the parallel session's guard found it. exp23 computes it, and it reproduces exactly.

claims.statement: At X = 4e5, with the trivial bound T(M) = sum_{m~M} #{x <= X : m | x^2+1} computed rather than assumed: T is FLAT at ~132,400 = 0.331 X across M = X/32 .. 8X, a factor of 256, constant to 0.1%. The saving T/S_mu is 12.38, 9.05, 6.57, 4.71, 3.43, 2.41, 1.79, 1.55, 1.42 against the predicted sqrt(X/M) of 5.66, 4.00, 2.83, 2.00, 1.41, 1.00, 0.71, 0.50, 0.35. BELOW theta = 1/2 the ratio observed/predicted is constant at 2.19-2.42, so the saving is 2.3 * sqrt(X/M). ABOVE it the ratio departs: 2.53, 3.09, 4.01. At theta = 1/2 exactly the saving is 2.41.
claims.notes: Run in-session over M from X divided by 32 up to 8X at X = 4e5, using exp16's mobius_of_x2plus1 sieve with the trivial bound accumulated alongside. The first measurement of sqrt-MX-law THROUGH its boundary; everything prior was below it (exp16 stops at M = X/2), so theta = 1/2 was an extrapolation from one side. Three results: T flat is the 'each x has O(1) divisors per dyadic band' fact measured rather than assumed; the constant 2.3 in saving = 2.3 sqrt(X/M) is new; and sqrt(X/M) genuinely stops applying above theta = 1/2 rather than degrading through it, which is what the law asserts and had not been checked. PRECISION the numbers force: 'the saving is exactly zero at theta = 1/2' is about the POWER and is correct (Q^{(1/2-theta)/2} = Q^0), but it does NOT mean S reaches the trivial bound -- the measured saving at M = X is 2.41, a constant factor. A reader could take 'no saving' as 'S = T', which is false by a factor of two and a half.

claims.statement: The trivial incidence count T(M) = sum_{m~M} #{x <= X : m | x^2+1} and the Cauchy-Schwarz diagonal DIAG = sum_x mu^2(x^2+1) #{m~M : m | x^2+1} are NOT the same object. At X = 2e5 over M = X/8 .. 2X, DIAG/T = 0.7658, 0.7649, 0.7651, 0.7681, 0.7658 -- constant across a factor of 16 in M, and NOT the plain squarefree density 0.8948. T = 0.331 X and DIAG = 0.253 X.
claims.notes: Run in-session with exp16's sieve, accumulating both counts over the same incidences. The gap between 0.765 and 0.8948 is a genuine correlation: among all (m,x) incidences with m in a dyadic band, only 76.5% have x^2+1 squarefree, against 89.5% among all x. So values of x^2+1 with more divisors in a band are MORE likely to be non-squarefree -- more prime factors at fixed size means smaller primes, and small primes are likelier to appear squared. WHY IT MATTERS: the parallel session's Cauchy-Schwarz reduction assumes DIAG ~ X as 'a standard divisor count', and saving-law-measured-through-theta-half measures T ~ X; the two constants differ by 24% and equating them would put that factor into a bound. Their measured DIAG ~ 5.05e4 at X = 2e5 is confirmed here independently at 5.07e4. CITATION CORRECTED -- a third instance of the same defect, found by running exp20 at the size the claims cite. It named exp16, which computes T but not DIAG; exp20 computes both. And the reproduced value differs because the SETUP differs and that is worth stating rather than smoothing: exp20 reports DIAG/T = 0.7761 at Q = 4e6 over the single band [2048, 4096), where X = 2000 makes that band N ~ X; this claim's 0.7658-0.7681 are at X = 2e5 over M = X/8 .. 2X, a different regime. Both say ~0.77 and neither is the squarefree density 0.8948, which is the content; the third digit is not comparable across the two setups and should not be quoted as if it were.

claims.statement: At X = 4e5 and M = X the Cauchy-Schwarz chain predicts the measured S_mu to 0.7%, using only constants measured independently and none fitted to the comparison. #m = 52187 and T = 132339 from the boundary run; DIAG/T = 0.7658 from the T-vs-DIAG run at X = 2e5; Cauchy-Schwarz tightness 0.75 measured by the parallel session at X = 2e5. Then sqrt(#m * DIAG) = 72725, and 0.75 * 72725 = 54544 against a measured 54955. Predicted saving T/S = 2.426 against a measured 2.408.
claims.notes: The chain is Cauchy-Schwarz (exact), Q2 = DIAG + OFF (exact), DIAG ~ X (measured, saving-law-measured-through-theta-half), #m ~ M/sqrt(log M) (Landau-Ramanujan), and OFF = o(DIAG) (measured, and equal to Chowla for this polynomial). Getting the VALUE to 0.7% -- not just the shape -- is a quantitative check on the whole decomposition, and it is a measurement of OFF as a by-product: the prediction used Q2 = DIAG, i.e. OFF = 0, so the 0.8% residual bounds OFF/DIAG at about 0.016 at this M, consistent with the parallel session's |OFF|/DIAG decaying to 0.038 at their largest M. Constants came from four separate runs at two values of X, on both sides of the collaboration; the agreement is therefore not self-consistency. MADE REPRODUCIBLE, and it strengthened. exp16 now computes the signed sum, the trivial bound and 0.75*sqrt(#m * 0.7658 T) alongside S_mod, where before it computed none of them and this claim cited it anyway. At X = 60000 the chain predicts S_mod at EVERY band, not only at M = X: 1698 vs 1702, 2355 vs 2541, 3268 vs 3258, 4549 vs 4540, 6338 vs 6293 -- within 1-7% across a factor of 16 in M. The original claim tested one band; the reproducible version tests five, which is what the experiments convention buys.

claims.statement: S_mu(M) saturates at DIAG = sum_x mu^2(x^2+1) d_M(x) ~ 0.253 X, not at |A| = X. At X = 2e5 over M = X .. 32X, S/DIAG = 0.5447, 0.7404, 0.8508, 0.9259, 0.9647, 0.9839 -- monotone to 1 -- while S/X reaches only 0.2494 and S/T only 0.7540, converging to DIAG/T = 0.7658. The mechanism is exact: for M >> X almost every modulus carries a single x, so its inner sum is one mu value and |sum| is 1 on squarefree x^2+1 and 0 otherwise, which counts squarefree incidences, which is DIAG.
claims.notes: Refines sqrt-MX-law's 'saturating at ~|A| for M >= X'. That is right to within a constant, since 0.253 X is of order X, but the ceiling is DIAG rather than |A| and the constant is 0.25 rather than 1 -- so 'saturating at |A|' read literally is wrong by a factor of four, in the same way 'the saving is exactly zero' read as S = T is wrong by 2.41. Both are true statements about orders whose literal readings are false, in one sentence of the same claim. Predicted before measuring, from the observation that a modulus with one x contributes |mu| in {0,1}; the prediction is what the run tested.

claims.statement: sum_{N(d)<=D} |r_d| ~ D/(2 pi) = 0.15915 D for A = {x+i : x <= X}, not ~ D. The constant is forced: r_d = 1 - r/q - theta with r/q and theta both roughly uniform, so r_d is triangular on (-1,1) and E|r_d| = int_0^1 2t(1-t) dt = 1/3; admissible (q,root) pairs of norm <= D number ~ (3/2pi) D; hence the sum is (1/3)(3/2pi) D = D/(2 pi). Measured 0.15895 at D = 5e5 against 0.159155 predicted, and per-ideal 0.33289 against 1/3 -- 0.13%.
claims.notes: Third instance of 'claims stated to an order, read as equalities', and the first in a `proved` claim: type-I-level said 'sum |r_d| ~ D', which is right about the order and off by 2 pi literally. Nothing downstream moves -- the argument needs the sum to be of order D, and a constant cannot turn D = o(X) into anything else -- so this pins the constant rather than correcting a conclusion. The two ingredients were already in the registry separately (|r_d| <= 1 and sharp, from type-I-level; the (3/2pi) density, from admissible-density) and neither claim could have carried constant 1 given the other.

claims.statement: sum_{x<=X} mu(x^2+1), sieved to X = 4e6: S = 134, -42, -208, -730, 482, 675 at X = 1e4, 4e4, 1.6e5, 6.4e5, 2.56e6, 4e6, giving |S|/sqrt(X) = 1.34, 0.21, 0.52, 0.91, 0.30, 0.34 -- bounded between 0.21 and 1.34 over more than two decades -- and |S|/X falling to 1.7e-4. Square-root cancellation, unmistakably.
claims.notes: Measured with exp16's sieve, which is cross-checked against sympy value by value. Scopes the sentence in Note M that the trivial bound 'has never been beaten by any amount, at any level, signed or absolute': that is about what is PROVED, and this is about what is TRUE. The estimate the repo needs at theta = 0 is not merely plausible but visibly correct, and the whole difficulty is that nobody can prove it -- which is a materially different position from a sequence that misbehaves. A reader taking the proof statement for a truth statement would conclude the opposite. Does NOT bear on chowla-for-x2plus1-is-open, which remains open: two decades of data is not an asymptotic, and this is exactly the extrapolation the `rigorous_finite` versus `extrapolated` distinction exists to prevent -- so no law is fitted here and none should be.

claims.statement: At X = 1e6, the SIGNED Type II sum sum_x mu(x^2+1) d_M(x) is -337, 588, -22, -750, 127, -497 over M = 512, 2048, 8192, 32768, 131072, 524288 -- a factor of 1024 in M -- giving |signed|/sqrt(T) = 0.59, 1.02, 0.04, 1.30, 0.22, 0.86, all O(1), with T essentially constant at 3.3e5 = 0.33 X. Over the same bands S_abs grows 3505 -> 97875, so signed/S_abs falls 0.096 -> 0.005.
claims.notes: Quantifies difficulty-is-the-absolute-values across a factor of 1024 in M, where that claim rested on a single 2% ratio at one band. The signed sum has FULL square-root cancellation relative to the incidence count, uniformly in M; the absolute-value sum has only the sqrt(X/M) saving and grows like sqrt(MX)/(log M)^{1/4}. So the ratio between them is not a constant 2% but a quantity that DECAYS as M grows -- the absolute value costs more the further into the Type II range one goes, which is the direction that matters since ASP's (B1) wants M large. T constant at 0.33 X independently reproduces saving-law-measured-through-theta-half's 0.331 X at a different X. The fluctuation of |signed|/sqrt(T) between 0.04 and 1.30 is what a random-sign sum of that size does and is not evidence of structure. MADE REPRODUCIBLE: exp16 now computes the signed sum, which it did not when this claim first cited it. At X = 60000 over M = 2048..32768, |signed|/sqrt(T) is 0.26, 0.13, 0.38, 0.65, 1.02 -- O(1) throughout, at a second X.

claims.statement: At X = 3000 the mean of G(n1,n2) is 1.7500, 0.6562, 0.2429, 0.0799, 0.0213 at N = 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048 taking n1 in [N,2N) and n2 over ALL cofactors with n1 < n2 < 2 n1 -- the faithful 'any dyadic band' reading, over 4, 64, 844, 12124, 163256 pairs. (The figures first recorded, 2.0, 0.667, 0.254, 0.0865, 0.0243, take BOTH cofactors from [N,2N), which is a strictly smaller population: 1, 21, 276, 4186, 56280 pairs. Every anchored value is higher, so the conclusion is better supported by the faithful reading than by the recorded one.) -- falling across that range, and NO CLEAN LAW IS CLAIMED for the decay: 1/N is wrong (the mean grows with X at fixed N: 0.2246, 0.2536, 0.2754 at N = 128 for X = 1500, 3000, 6000), and (log X)/N is wrong too (mean*N/log X is 4.05 at N = 128 but 5.6 at N = 512 and 7.8 at N = 8192, drifting). The values are what is claimed -- while max G is 2 at every band. So for N >> 1 the expected Gram entry is far below 1 while G itself is an integer taking only the values 0, 1, 2. At N ~ 2048 the mean is 0.024 against a granularity of 1: the quantity a dispersion argument would call the error is FORTY TIMES the quantity it would call the main term. ANCHORED-BAND CAVEAT: the means quoted here come from bands [N,2N) with N stepped by powers of two or four, which never forms a pair like (9,17) of ratio 1.89. Re-measured by RATIO (cofactor pairs with n2 < 2*n1, which is what 'one dyadic band' means) at Q = 9e6, the means are 1.7500, 1.1667, 0.6562, 0.4530, 0.2429, 0.1455, 0.0799, 0.0404, 0.0213 at N = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, over 4, 18, 64, 234, 844, 3237, 12124, 44287, 163256 pairs. LOWER at every sieve-relevant scale over roughly three times the population, so the conclusion is unchanged and slightly better supported; the U's argmin stays at N = 4096 = 1.37X. See experiments/exp20_gram_mean.py::anchored_vs_ratio.
claims.notes: The quantitative form of 'there is no main term to extract', which the repo has carried qualitatively. Dispersion needs count = main term + error with the error genuinely smaller; here the main term is 0.024 and the count is an integer, so 'main term + smaller error' is not a decomposition that exists. This is stronger than c4-free as an argument against dispersion, because it does not depend on the bound being exactly 1 or exactly 2 -- any bounded integer-valued count with mean o(1) has the same problem. A naive independence heuristic gives mean G = rho(n1)rho(n2)/N and the observed mean is 5-6 times that, stable across bands; the CONSTANT is not to be trusted (the heuristic uses the mean of rho rather than the mean of the product, and pairs sharing a modulus are correlated), but the 1/N SHAPE is what the argument needs and it holds. Run in-session from a divisor-built incidence table; max G = 2 independently reproduces rational-gram-bounded-on-windows. CORRECTION, same day: the first version said the mean falls like 1/N, measured at a SINGLE X = 3000. Checking the X-dependence at fixed N shows it grows, roughly like log X: at N = 128 the mean is 0.2246, 0.2536, 0.2754 for X = 1500, 3000, 6000, and mean*N/log X is flat at 3.93, 4.05, 4.05. At N = 512 the same quantity is 5.10, 5.53, 5.62, still drifting, so the constant is not clean and only the log X shape is claimed. THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED and the margin is large: the argument needs mean << 1 while the count is an integer, and 0.024 at N = 2048 has a log X in it either way. Recorded because a law fitted at one X is the same failure as a law fitted from one side of a boundary, which this repo made twice today. SECOND CORRECTION, same day. Having found 1/N wrong I replaced it with (log X)/N, on a constant that was flat at ONE band (4.05 at N = 128) and visibly drifting at another (5.6 at N = 512) -- which I recorded at the time and then quoted as a law anyway. The parallel session's cofactor-side numbers extend the drift to 7.8 at N = 8192 and the fitted exponent moves between 0.80 and 0.88 with the range. So NO clean power or log-power fits, and none is claimed; the measured values reproduce exactly between two independent constructions and those are the claim. Twice in one evening I fitted a law to a decay that does not have one, which is what the extrapolated status exists to stop and what rigorous_finite is for instead. ANCHORED-BAND DEFECT, audited and survived: the bands above are [N,2N) with N stepped by powers of four, so a pair like (9,17) of ratio 1.89 is never formed -- 'one dyadic band' means ratio < 2. Re-measured with n1 in [N,2N) and n2 ranging over all cofactors with n1 < n2 < 2*n1 at Q = 9e6: means 1.7500, 0.6562, 0.2429, 0.0799, 0.0213 at N = 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048 against the anchored 2.0000, 0.6667, 0.2536, 0.0865, 0.0243, over 4, 64, 844, 12124, 163256 pairs against 1, 21, 276, 4186, 56280. The ratio means are LOWER at every sieve-relevant scale over roughly three times the population, so the mean-o(1) conclusion is unchanged and slightly better supported, and the U-shape survives (0.0171 at N = 8192, climbing to 0.5400 at N = 2097152). claims.statement: POSITIVE CONTROL for the-main-term-is-smaller-than-the-granularity. claims.statement: Ford-Maynard's footnote 2 (p.7) asks for '#{n : n m_1, n m_2 in J} with an error term better than O(1) on average over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}'. At c = 1/2 that range is m_1, m_2 ~ x^eps. The mean of G over a cofactor band [N,2N) falls like (log X)/N (the-main-term-is-smaller-than-the-granularity), so at N = x^eps the mean is (log x)/x^eps -- still tending to 0 for every fixed eps > 0 -- while G is a non-negative integer equal to 0 for almost every pair. An error genuinely below 1 therefore PINS THE VALUE: at this density their requirement is not an estimation problem but a request to determine G exactly.
claims.notes: REFUTED the same day, by the parallel session, and the error is a direction. The footnote averages over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}, which at c = 1/2 is x^eps -- and SMALL eps means SMALL moduli: at x = 1.44e8, x^0.05 = 2.6 and x^0.10 = 6.5. I read N = x^eps as large and concluded the mean was small there. It is the opposite end. Measured at X = 12000, mean G is 2.000, 1.333, 0.810, 0.577 at N = 8, 16, 32, 64, i.e. >= 1 for eps <~ 0.18, and below eps ~ 0.11 the band holds at most one cofactor so the average is over an empty set. So 'an error below 1 pins the value' does not follow at the footnote's range as eps -> 0, which is where the footnote's eps lives. WHAT SURVIVES: fm-barrier-is-unconditional-at-density-half (the hypothesis is vacuous at c = 1/2) and the-main-term-is-smaller-than-the-granularity in the range the SIEVE uses, which is the point -- see fm-barrier-range-is-small-moduli.

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard's footnote 2 averages over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}, which at c = 1/2 is x^eps -- SMALL moduli as eps -> 0, not large. Measured at X = 12000: mean G = 2.000, 1.333, 0.810, 0.577 over N = 8, 16, 32, 64, with 2, 4, 7, 13 cofactors in the band respectively. So the mean is >= 1 for eps <~ 0.18, and below eps ~ 0.11 the band holds at most one cofactor and the average is over an empty set. The mean of G is U-shaped in N, bottoming near N ~ X and rising again as the cofactors grow large enough that only a few tiny moduli exist and every pair shares them.
claims.notes: Refutes fm-barrier-asks-for-G-exactly, which read the footnote's range as large moduli. Found by the parallel session and verified here: at x = 1.44e8, x^0.05 = 2.6 and x^0.10 = 6.5. TWO CAUTIONS on the small-N end. The averages there are over 1 to 13 pairs, so they are the informative-subset problem in its own right -- a 'mean' over one pair is not an average. And the full-graph maximum at small N is 3, at G(17,26) with shared moduli 1, 85, 2966965 (verified here directly), but one of those is the UNIT cofactor m = 1, which full-graph-growth-is-pell already records as inadmissible in a Type II hypothesis where both variables are confined to ranges; excluding it gives 2. WHAT IS UNAFFECTED, and it is the load-bearing part: ASP's (B1) forces M >= sqrt(x) = X, so the cofactor n = (x^2+1)/m is at most X -- exactly the range where the mean is small and falling. The rise, the max-3 and the small-N regime all sit outside what the sieve uses. THE '>= 1' LINE IS NOT FORD-MAYNARD'S, and this claim should not be read as if it were. Checked at source: footnote 2, p. 7 of arXiv:2407.14368v1 asks for "estimating #{n : nm_1, nm_2 in J} with an error term better than O(1) on average over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}". That is a condition on the ERROR TERM, not on the mean exceeding any threshold. The numbers here -- mean G = 2.000, 1.333, 0.810, 0.577 at N = 8, 16, 32, 64 -- are a correct measurement of this repo's own quantity, and '>= 1 for eps <~ 0.18' is a description of them, not a statement about what the footnote requires. Note F already records the correct reading and has since it was written: the count is 0 or 1, so the error term IS O(1) and no averaging can improve it, which is why 'typically very difficult' becomes impossible here. Flagged because the parallel session read this claim as recording '>= 1' as the relevant line and asked whether that was the source or a paraphrase. It is a paraphrase, and it had drifted far enough to be quoted back. The repo's rule that nothing protects the paraphrase, applied to the one place it matters most -- a claim standing between a measurement and a cited paper.

claims.statement: The mean of G over cofactor bands is U-shaped in N and its minimum sits at N = 1.37 X at both X = 3000 and X = 6000, with min mean G = 0.01319 and 0.00827. The balanced split of the bilinear form is n = m = sqrt(x^2+1) ~ X, so the Gram mean is smallest exactly where the Type II sum lives. The minimum also DEEPENS with X, 0.01319 -> 0.00827 for a doubling. The RIGHT arm is a function of N/X^2: at X = 3000 and X = 6000 the values 0.09041/0.09041, 0.23767/0.23830, 0.51416/0.51446 coincide at equal N/X^2, three to four digits. The LEFT arm is NOT a function of N/X -- at N/X = 0.34 it is 0.0466 against 0.0296 -- nor of N alone, since at fixed N it grows about 11% per doubling of X. No scaling variable is claimed for it.
claims.notes: Found by the parallel session on a cofactor-side construction; verified here from a divisor-built incidence table, an independent construction. Both argmins land on N = 1.37 X (bands are dyadic, so the resolution is a factor 2 and what is measured is that it stays in the same band RELATIVE TO X across a factor 2 in X), and the minimum values agree to five digits. Why it matters more than 'the mean is small': the smallness is ALIGNED WITH THE APPLICATION rather than incidental to it -- the obstruction is strongest precisely at the split the Type II sum uses, and it strengthens as X grows. Structural account of the U: at N << X the cofactors are small so each has many moduli and pairs collide; at N >> X the moduli are few and tiny so every pair shares them; the balanced split is where both sides are maximally spread. NO LAW is attached to either arm -- see the-main-term-is-smaller-than-the-granularity, where two attempts to fit the decay were withdrawn. CORRECTION: the first version claimed the left arm was controlled by N/X. It is not, and MY OWN PRINTED TABLE showed it -- 0.04657 at (X=3000, N=1024) against 0.02958 at (X=6000, N=2048), both N/X = 0.34. Caught by the parallel session. That is the THIRD law fitted to this one decay tonight and the third to fail: 1/N, (log X)/N, and now N/X for the left arm. Each time the values reproduced exactly between two independent constructions and the law did not, which is the finding: this quantity is reproducible and unparameterised, and the reflex to name its shape has cost four corrections. THE STRUCTURAL CONCLUSION IS UNTOUCHED because it rests on the ARGMIN, not on either arm's law -- argmin/X = 1.37 at X = 3000, 6000, 12000 from two constructions -- and so does the explanation, which never needed a clean power.

claims.statement: The cofactor bands measured are exactly the range ASP's (B1) admits for its inner variable. In ASP's normalisation x = Q, so sqrt(x) = X, and with the level capped at D <= Q^{1/2} = X (Note B) the range Delta^{-1} sqrt(D) < N < delta^{-1} sqrt(x) is roughly sqrt(X) < N < X -- at X = 3000, N from 55 to 3000. Measured mean G there, over cofactor pairs of RATIO < 2 (which is what 'one dyadic band' means): 0.1455, 0.0799, 0.0404, 0.0213 at N = 256, 512, 1024, 2048, falling monotonically and never above 0.15, over 3237, 12124, 44287 and 163256 pairs. (The anchored-band values this claim used to lead with are 0.1596, 0.0865, 0.0466, 0.0243 over 1128, 4186, 15051 and 56280 pairs -- higher at every scale over roughly a third of the population, so the faithful reading supports the conclusion BETTER than the recorded one did.) The U's argmin at N = 1.37 X sits just ABOVE the top of the admissible range, so within (B1) the mean is falling throughout and is smallest at the top. See experiments/exp20_gram_mean.py::anchored_vs_ratio for both columns.
claims.notes: Ties the-main-term-is-smaller-than-the-granularity to the hypothesis it bears on, rather than leaving it as a fact about arbitrary bands. The n in G(n_1,n_2) IS (B)'s inner variable: dispersion opens the square over m and produces sum over n_1, n_2 of G(n_1,n_2), so (B1) is exactly the constraint on those n. Delta and delta are absorbed as constants, hence 'roughly'. The point is that no part of the admissible range escapes: mean G is below 0.16 across all of it and an integer count has no decomposition into main term plus smaller error anywhere in there. The rise at N >> X and the max of 3 at small N both sit outside, which is why fm-barrier-range-is-small-moduli's corrections do not reach this.

claims.statement: At Q = 4e6 over the band N in [2048,4096): x^2+1 has kappa 1.00 and mean G 0.0219 (max 2); a^2+b^6 has kappa 115.4 and mean G 0.5590 (max 22); a^2+b^4 has kappa 1297.5 and mean G 3.592 (max 107); a^2+(b^2+1)^2 has kappa 1269.3 and mean G 12.809 (max 97). So mean G exceeds 1 for both sequences KNOWN to capture their primes and falls below 1 for x^2+1, while kappa does not separate them: a^2+b^6 has kappa >> 1 with mean below 1, and a^2+b^4 and a^2+(b^2+1)^2 have nearly equal kappa (1297 vs 1269) with means differing by 3.6x. Max G does not separate them either -- 2, 22, 107, 97 puts a^2+b^6 between the captured pair.
claims.notes: Gives Note K's 'kappa is necessary and not sufficient' a candidate for the sufficient part, with the interpretation from the-main-term-is-smaller-than-the-granularity: mean G > 1 says a main term exists for dispersion to decompose. A PREDICTION, NOT A CONFIRMATION -- four sequences, one band, one Q, and two of the four are the pair the observation was built from (mean-G-separates-x2plus1-from-a2b4). The content is the other two. a^2+b^6 sits at 0.559, below the line, and THIS REPO HAS READ NO SOURCE ON ITS STATUS: kappa-invariant covers a^2+b^{2k} for k = 2..6 as a kappa measurement only, and the repo's non-negotiable forbids asserting a literature outcome from memory. If a^2+b^6 is captured somewhere, this is refuted; if open, it is one point of independent support. Someone should read a source before this is quoted as more than a pattern in four numbers. REFUTED WITHIN THE HOUR, by the test designed to confirm it. x^3+2y^3 is CAPTURED (Heath-Brown) and has mean G = 0.1888 at the same band -- below 1, and LOWER than a^2+b^6's 0.5590. So 'mean G > 1 for the captured sequences' fails, and the ordering fails too. The four-point pattern was a coincidence of the two sequences it was built from.

claims.statement: Friedlander-Iwaniec, in the a^2+b^4 paper, p.952: 'Further interesting connections to elliptic curves hold for primes of the form 27a^2 + 4b^6 and there is some hope to produce such primes using our arguments in the domain Z[zeta_3].'
claims.citation: Friedlander-Iwaniec, 'The polynomial X^2+Y^4 captures its primes', Annals of Math. 148 (1998), p.952
claims.notes: 'Some hope to produce' is not a result: as of that paper the b^6 shape was a target the authors thought their method might reach and had not. Relevant to mean-G-crosses-one-where-kappa-does-not, whose one below-the-line sequence with no known outcome is a^2+b^6 at mean G 0.559. Density matches: a << Q^{1/2}, b << Q^{1/6} gives |A| ~ Q^{2/3} and kappa ~ Q^{1/3} = 158 at Q = 4e6, against 115 measured. DOES NOT SETTLE THE CURRENT STATUS -- 27a^2+4b^6 is not literally a^2+b^6, and a 1998 remark says nothing about 2026 -- so the classifier's prediction stays a prediction. What it does establish is that the sequence the classifier puts below the line is one the authors of the method that captured its neighbour singled out as not yet done. Found by grepping the repo's own PDFs, which is how the repo's rule against asserting literature status from memory is supposed to be discharged.

claims.statement: Mean G does NOT separate sequences that capture their primes from those that do not. At Q = 4e6, band N in [2048,4096): x^3+2y^3, CAPTURED by Heath-Brown, has kappa 75.1 and mean G 0.1888 with max G 79; a^2+b^6, not known captured, has kappa 115.4 and mean G 0.5590 with max G 22. The captured sequence has the LOWER mean, and it is below 1. Full table: x^2+1 0.0219, x^3+2y^3 0.1888, a^2+b^6 0.5590, a^2+b^4 3.5920, a^2+(b^2+1)^2 12.8086 -- captured sequences at 0.19, 3.59 and 12.81, non-captured at 0.02 and 0.56, interleaved.
claims.notes: Refutes mean-G-crosses-one-where-kappa-does-not, which was recorded about an hour earlier and reached both Note K and the CLAUDE.md fallback. The refuting test was chosen precisely because it was decisive: x^3+2y^3 and a^2+b^6 both have |A| ~ Q^{2/3} hence kappa ~ Q^{1/3}, so kappa CANNOT distinguish them and a real classifier had to. Mean G does not. WHAT SURVIVES is the narrow original observation, mean-G-separates-x2plus1-from-a2b4: the argument that a bounded integer count with mean o(1) has no main term does not prove too much, because a^2+b^4 has mean 3.59 at the band where x^2+1 has 0.022. That is a two-sequence control and was never a classifier; generalising it to a four-sequence law was the error, and it was built from two points and 'confirmed' on two more of which one had no known outcome. SOURCE FOR THE REFUTING POINT, since the whole refutation rests on x^3+2y^3 being captured and asserting that from memory would be the repo's first non-negotiable violated in the act of enforcing another: hb-alpha-hierarchy cites Heath-Brown, 'Primes represented by x^3+2y^3', Acta Math. 186 (2001) -- the title is the theorem -- and hb-level and hb-R1-not-met corroborate from the same paper. Not taken from memory. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON the classifier was wrong, visible once exp20 made it reproducible at a second Q: the threshold is not stable in Q. At Q = 2.5e5 even a^2+b^4 sits at 0.8200, below 1, while at Q = 4e6 it is 3.5920. So 'mean G > 1' does not name a fixed property of a sequence at all -- it names a property of a sequence AT A Q. That alone should have killed it before the x^3+2y^3 test, and it was invisible while the numbers lived in a scratchpad script run once.

claims.statement: Theorem O.3''. A dyadic window contains (xi, tau_1 xi, tau_k xi) with k >= 2 only if (4k + sqrt(16k^2+2))(2c+1) < c(kc - c - 1), where c = gcd(M, 2X). O.3' discards a term at rho^2 < 9/8 - rho/(8k) by using rho > 0; rho > 1 is free (U_k > 2k sqrt(ab) > 2ka gives rho > 0, and Lambda > 0 with rho^2 < 1 would force rho > k >= 1). Keeping it gives rho^2 < 1 + (k-1)/A_k, A_k = 4k + sqrt(16k^2+2). k -> infinity recovers c >= 17, so O.3' is the k-free shadow; k = 2 needs c >= 34, k = 3 needs c >= 26, c = 17 needs k >= 35. k = 1 must be excluded: there U_1 = a+b, rho = 1 exactly and Lambda = 0/0.
claims.notes: Strengthens O.3' inside a family O.3' already covered; it does NOT touch the p,q >= 2 gap that keeps O.2 open, since it still assumes tau_1 acts. The sharpened rho bound is essentially saturated -- the tightest of 204 in-window k >= 2 multipliers over a <= 8, b <= 30000 sits at 0.9998 of it -- so little more is available by this route. Exact form of the integrality step: with g = c*rho in Z, M(g-c)(g+c) = 4kac(kc-g), and A_k t(2c+t) < c(kc-c-t) for g = c+t reduces to t = 1 by monotonicity. Deliberately depends on nothing: the derivation is standalone algebra and does not rest on O.3''s independent verification -- the dependency guard rejected the first version for claiming otherwise.

claims.statement: Every acting in-window multiplier with k >= 2 on a REALISED ratio class has c = gcd(M, 2X) in {2, 4}: (c,k) = (2,12), (2,33), (2,91) at X = 3000 and additionally (4,4) at X = 4000. Against Theorem O.3'''s threshold of 17 that is two orders of magnitude of slack, so O.3'' is nowhere near binding on what actually occurs.
claims.notes: This measures the HYPOTHESIS on configurations that do occur, not the conclusion on configurations that never do, so it is not blocked by triples-cannot-be-settled-by-measurement. What it shows is negative for the theorem's relevance: the constraint that actually forbids triples in nature is not this one.

claims.statement: kappa carries no information beyond the density exponent. With |A| = Q^alpha, kappa = |A|^2/Q = Q^{2 alpha - 1} identically, so kappa > 1 <=> alpha > 1/2, kappa = 1 <=> alpha = 1/2, and sqrt(kappa) = Q^{alpha - 1/2}. Every kappa threshold is an alpha threshold in different units.
claims.notes: Recorded because the repo presents alpha and 'kappa > 1?' as SEPARATE columns in Note D's ledger, and Note K's headline 'kappa > 1 is necessary and not sufficient' reads as a finding about kappa when it is the statement 'density above 1/2 is necessary and not sufficient' -- which is the literature's own boundary, and Xiannan Li's record is 0.6418. This does not weaken any argument: kappa = 1 => forest is a real statement about the incidence graph at alpha = 1/2, and sqrt-kappa-is-the-poisson-length gives kappa a second reading as the Poisson range. What it forbids is treating a kappa observation as INDEPENDENT evidence for a density conclusion or vice versa. Prompted by the note-K adversarial-review bullet observing that kappa, like the refuted mean-G classifier, is a statistic fitted to a handful of sequences with known outcomes -- the difference being that kappa's threshold is an identity rather than a fit, which is why it survives and the classifier did not.

claims.statement: Theorem O.4. Three shared moduli of the class (a,b) lie in one dyadic window only if tau_min^4 < 2 + 1/X_1^2, where X_1 = sqrt(a m_1 - 1) is the smallest and tau_min = min{tau > 1 : tau = (U+V sqrt D)/M, U^2 - D V^2 = M^2}. UNLIKE O.3, O.3' and O.3'' it assumes nothing about which multiplier acts, so it reaches the p,q >= 2 gap. Proof: the automorph X_j = (U X_i + V a Y_i)/M plus a Y_i > X_i sqrt(D) gives the exact X_j > tau_V X_i; composing two steps gives X_3 > tau_min^2 X_1; and m = (X^2+1)/a turns that into m_3/m_1 > (tau_min^4 X_1^2 + 1)/(X_1^2 + 1). Since |V| >= 2 unless a^2-ab+b^2 is a perfect square, tau_min = tau_1 and the threshold is b/a > 53.694 at X_1 = 1, rising to b/a > [(1+sqrt2)(1+sqrt2+2^(5/4))]^2 = 133.8747813 as m_1 -> infinity, i.e. M > 4(2^(1/4)+2^(3/4)) sqrt(ab) = 11.48400 sqrt(ab). The pair threshold is b/a > (1+sqrt2)^4 = 33.9706, and t_triple = t_pair + 2^(5/4)(1+sqrt2).
claims.notes: The finite term is load-bearing, not decoration: the modulus ratio is tau^2 only asymptotically, and the clean form m_{i+2}/m_i >= tau_1^4 is FALSE -- 9 violations in 110 gaps at X = 4000, tightest at (1,5) m 2 -> 65 where 32.50 sits under tau_1^4 = 46.98. With the correction, 0 violations in 110, and sharp: at (1,5) m 20737 -> 974170 the bound is 46.9765 against 46.9774. Step 2 must go through the automorph -- bounding |V| = M(X_j^2-X_i^2)/(X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j) instead yields tau at V/a, true but not sharp for a > 1. Slightly stronger than the determinant route, AND it repairs that route's recorded constant. Note O had the Plucker-parity argument yielding M/sqrt(D) >= 11.484 unconditionally; it does not. With the exact |V| < (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R), |V| >= 4 and R < sqrt2 give 8 sqrt2 = 11.3137, and the finite form R^2 < 2 + 1/X_1^2 gives only 6.93 at X_1 = 1 (9.60, 10.46, 10.99, 11.23 at X_1 = 2,3,5,10). 11.484 is right but comes from O.4, where 2^(1/4) enters from the composite tau_1^2 < sqrt2 rather than from |V| >= 4 -- and the two expressions are algebraically identical, since 1/(2^(1/4) - 2^(-1/4)) = 2^(1/4)(sqrt2+1) = 2^(1/4) + 2^(3/4). It is a NECESSARY condition, not a contradiction: O.2 stays open, and O.4 is not binding -- among classes clearing b/a > 133.87 with three moduli the smallest two-step ratio is 14.50 at (1,533), a factor 7.25 from a window.

claims.statement: Theorem O.5. No dyadic window contains (xi, tau_p xi, tau_p^2 xi), for any p >= 1 PROVIDED X_1 >= 1, with no hypothesis on M, on a, or on which multipliers act. X_1 = 0 means a = 1 and m_1 = 1, where the window [1,2) holds a single modulus, so that case is vacuous rather than open -- stated explicitly because Prop O.1 was false as written for omitting its hypothesis. Proof: tau_p^2 = (U' + V' sqrt D)/M with U' = M + 8p^2 D/M, so tau_p^2 in T requires M | 8p^2 D; D = a(a+M) == a^2 mod M and gcd(a,M) = gcd(a,b) = 1 for a reduced class, so M | 8p^2 and M <= 8p^2. Theorem O.4 with X_1 >= 1 gives tau_p^4 < 3, hence p < 0.139060 M/sqrt(D) and 8p^2 < 0.154701 M^2/D, forcing D < M -- but M = b-a < b <= ab = D always. At p = 1 the divisibility is an equivalence: tau_1^2 in T <=> M | 8.
claims.notes: SUPERSEDES Proposition O.1, which is the p = 1 case and needed the auxiliary a g^2 < M with g = gcd(U,V), a window hypothesis, and an escape clause. O.5 explains the escape instead of tolerating it: at (a,b) = (1,5), M = 4 | 8, so tau_1^2 genuinely IS in T -- O.1's inequality failing there by nothing (a g^2 = 4 = M exactly) was the symptom, and the cause is that the integrality is fine and the WINDOW is what fails. Verified: 0 failures over 555 occurrences of tau_p^2 in T with a <= 60, b <= 4000, p <= 30; the p = 1 equivalence over 133,670 coprime pairs. The two realised classes where tau_1^2 acts at X = 3000 are (1,5) with M = 4 and (1,2) with M = 1. WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH is p != q: the composite's integrality M | U_p U_q + 4pq D does not collapse -- multiplying by the conjugate returns M | M^2(M^2 + 4(p^2+q^2)D), true for free. So O.2's surviving case is exactly two DISTINCT multipliers, and nothing realised exhibits it.

Its step (1) -- consecutive solutions satisfy U^2 - D V^2 = M^2 with V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i -- holds over consecutive pairs at two sizes -- 1596 at X = 2500 and 1950 at X = 3000, zero failures at both (the count is size-dependent and excludes X_i = 0) at X = 2500 with ZERO failures, built from ratio_classes so that 'consecutive' is consecutive in the sorted modulus list and therefore crosses orbits.
