claims.statement: Proposition O.6. For M = b-a an odd prime, exactly one of M | S, M | T holds at each solution (S = X+Y, T = X-Y), and it forces the sign of U_p == eps_p 2pa: M | S => M | B_p, M | T => M | A_p. The exact identities are M S' = A_p S + V_p M X and M T' = B_p T - V_p M X, and in subcase A, A_p beta = M + 4p^2 a with A_p == 4pa forces beta == p (mod M), so T' == 2X(beta - p) == 0. THE SUBCASE THEREFORE ALTERNATES AT EVERY STEP. Consequently a triple has eps_p = +1 and eps_q = -1, and both of the composite's integrality conditions become automatic: q U_p + p U_q == 0 and U_p U_q + 4pq D == 0 (mod M). So THOSE TWO CONDITIONS carry no information. (CORRECTED: this first read 'so the integrality route cannot close O.2', which is too strong -- the alternation is itself a consistency constraint and Theorem O.7 closes the M odd prime case with it.)
claims.notes: CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR. Filed as 'the integrality route cannot close O.2'; the evidence showed only that the COMPOSITE'S INTEGRALITY CONDITIONS are vacuous. Generalising 'sub-route X-prime is dead' to 'route X is dead' is this repo's most repeated error, and theorem-O7-M-odd-prime uses this very proposition to close the case. The measurements below all stand. Verified at X = 3000 over M odd prime: 246 steps, alternates 246 times and stays the same 0 times; eps forced by the subcase and beta == p (resp. alpha == -p) with 0 failures; and 0 failures over 493 opposite-sign (p,q) pairs against 40 of 246 same-sign pairs FAILING both conditions -- so the conditions have content and the alternation is what removes it. THE NAIVE IDENTITY IS WRONG: S' = A_p S / M, which the mod-M relation suggests, fails on 246 of 246 pairs; only M S' = A_p S + V_p M X holds. The necessary conditions M | A_p S and M | B_p T survive that error, the orbit bookkeeping does not, and the first version of this argument was built on the wrong form. NOT VACUOUS: M odd prime is 54 of the 379 realised close pairs (14%), so what fails is the method, not the coverage. This is the mechanism behind the recorded empirical observation that all 95 candidates are satisfiable mod M -- for M odd prime that is now a proof, and it says why.

claims.statement: For a line A_c = {a + ci : a >= 1, a^2 + c^2 <= Q}: |A_c| = isqrt(Q - c^2), so kappa = |A|^2/Q = 1 - c^2/Q -- exactly 1 in the limit, FOR EVERY c. A single line cannot have kappa > 1; the geometry forbids it. And A_c is C4-free by Note F's argument with c in place of 1: (a1+ci)(a4+ci) = (a2+ci)(a3+ci) gives a1 a4 = a2 a3 and a1 + a4 = a2 + a3, hence {a1,a4} = {a2,a3}. Two lines always admit a 4-cycle: at (c1,c2) = (2,3), which has no c = 1 and neither c dividing the other, (1+2i)(6+2i) = 2+14i = (2+2i)(4+3i). Checked over (2,3), (2,5), (3,5), (3,7), (5,7), (4,6) and over single lines c = 1,2,3,5,7 at Q = 1e6.
claims.notes: Explains why kappa and C4-freeness cross at the same threshold in Note K's A_B family instead of leaving it as a coincidence that argues FOR kappa: kappa = |B|^2 counts the lines and C4-freeness permits one, so the two conditions are functions of the same integer. The sharpness is real and is not evidence that a density statistic detects 4-cycles. It also generalises Note F: the C4-free lemma is not a fact about x^2+1, it is a fact about a line, and x^2+1 is the case c = 1. Which sharpens the obstruction rather than softening it -- x^2+1 is not unluckily C4-free, every line is, and alpha = 1/2 is forced for all of them. Does NOT depend on c4-freeness-is-arithmetic-not-density, though it is the obvious neighbour: that claim is a measurement and this is algebra, and the dependency guard rejected the edge for exactly that reason -- a proved claim cannot rest on a rigorous_finite one. The guard was right; I had listed a related result as a premise.

claims.statement: Theorem O.7. For M = b-a an odd prime, no dyadic window contains three shared moduli of the class (a,b) -- Conjecture O.2 on that slice, assuming nothing about which multipliers act, so it covers p != q. Proof: the exact identity a|V|(X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j) = M(X_j^2 - X_i^2) with Y > X sqrt(b/a) gives |V| < (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R), R = X_j/X_i; a window with X_i >= 1 gives R^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2 <= 3, so |V| < 0.57735 M/sqrt(D) <= 0.40825 M < M and M nmid V. That is the only hypothesis Proposition O.6's alternation needs, so all three pairwise steps of a triple flip the subcase. xi_1 -> xi_2 -> xi_3 flips twice, putting xi_3 in subcase A; the single step xi_1 -> xi_3 flips once, putting it in B; the dichotomy forbids both.
claims.notes: THE HYPOTHESIS IS SHARP AND THE ESCAPE IS OBSERVED. M nmid V is all the proof needs, and every realised M-odd-prime class holding three moduli has M | V on its two-step: (2,13) M=11 V=110; (2,5) M=3 V=18; (2,25) M=23 V=322. Those triples sit at ratios of 1e4 and up, which is how |V| gets past 0.57735 M/sqrt(D). Over all pairs with M odd prime at X = 6000, 454 of 459 flip the subcase and ALL 5 that do not have M | V. Verified at X = 6000: identity 0 failures over 4033 pairs; in-window bound 0 failures over 751 pairs with max |V|sqrt(D)/M = 0.3529; M | V occurs 0 times in-window; dichotomy and flip 0 failures over 90 in-window M-odd-prime pairs. THE FACTOR a IN THE IDENTITY IS LOAD-BEARING and I dropped it first -- 3389 of 4033 pairs failed until it was restored, and with it the bound comes out with no a at all. WHAT REMAINS OPEN IS M COMPOSITE: the dichotomy and the sign both use primality, since U^2 == (Va)^2 gives only M | A_V B_V in general and the signs can differ across the factorisation -- the same 2-adic gap O.3 had. M odd prime is 54 of the 379 realised close pairs (14%), so this is a real slice.

claims.statement: Adjoining exactly two Gaussian integers to the line destroys C4-freeness without moving kappa. For A = {x+i : x <= X} u {2+2i, 4+2i}, kappa = (X+2)^2/(X^2+1) -> 1 -- 1.000004 at X = 1e6, indistinguishable from the bare line's 0.999999 -- while (1+i)(4+2i) = 2+6i = (2+i)(2+2i) is a 4-cycle. So the coincidence of thresholds in Note K's A_B family is a property of that parameterisation, not of kappa: O(1) elements flip C4-freeness at fixed kappa.
claims.notes: STATED NARROWLY ON PURPOSE, and the narrowing is the honest part. This shows kappa cannot see the BINARY property C4-free/not. It does NOT show kappa fails to track the QUANTITY of 4-cycles: one cycle moves max G from 1 to 2 and leaves mean G at O(1/X), and this repo's own measurements (mean-G-does-not-classify, gram-mean-is-minimal-at-the-balanced-split) say mean G is the load-bearing statistic and max G is not. So this refines Note K's 'must not be demoted on these grounds' -- it supplies other grounds -- and leaves the Type II obstruction untouched, which is a statement about the whole graph. Recorded this way because the tempting version, 'kappa is blind to the obstruction', would be the same over-reading that put two claims in this registry as refuted.

claims.statement: Theorem O.7's two load-bearing steps, derived from scratch and re-measured. IDENTITY: a*V*(X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j) = M(X_i^2 - X_j^2). Proof: V(X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j) = X_i^2 Y_j^2 - X_j^2 Y_i^2; substituting Y^2 = X^2 + M m (from b m - a m = M m) gives M(X_i^2 m_j - X_j^2 m_i), and m = (X^2+1)/a turns that into M(X_i^2 - X_j^2)/a. BOUND: Y > X sqrt(b/a) since Y^2 = (b/a)(X^2+1) - 1 > (b/a)X^2, so X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j > 2 X_i X_j sqrt(b/a) and |V| < M(R - 1/R)/(2 sqrt D) with R = X_j/X_i. In-window with X_i >= 1, R^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2 <= 3, giving |V| < 0.57735 M/sqrt(D), and sqrt(D) >= sqrt 2 gives |V| < 0.40825 M < M, so M does not divide V. Measured at X = 6000: identity 0 failures / 3814 consecutive pairs; in-window bound 0 failures / 751 with max |V| sqrt(D)/M = 0.3529; M | V in-window for M an odd prime occurs 0 times; and 0 in-window triples with M an odd prime, which is O.7's conclusion.
claims.notes: Verified from the other side: I derived the identity algebraically before running anything, which is what makes this independent rather than a re-run. The three escape triples reproduce exactly -- (2,13) M=11, m 5 -> 48985, V13 = 110 = 10M; (2,5) M=3, 13 -> 18241, V13 = 18 = 6M; (2,25) M=23, 13 -> 499001, V13 = 322 = 14M -- and they escape at modulus ratios of 1e4 and up, which is exactly how |V| gets past a bound that is only valid in-window. My pair count is 3814 against their 4033; I skip X_i = 0 and they appear not to, and the conclusion is unaffected either way. The factor a in the identity is load-bearing -- they report 3389 of 4033 failing without it -- and it cancels out of the final bound entirely, which is the kind of thing that looks like an error until derived. No dependency on O.4, though I listed one and the guard rejected it: R^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2 follows from the window condition alone -- m_j < 2 m_i gives a m_j - 1 < 2(a m_i - 1) + 1 -- and O.4 is not needed. Second time tonight the dependency guard caught me listing a neighbouring result as a premise; both times the claim was proved and the neighbour was not, which is exactly the ordering it enforces.

claims.statement: For M odd SQUAREFREE and any in-window consecutive pair, some prime p | M has p not dividing V. Proof: if every p | M divided V then M = rad(M) would divide V, and O.7's in-window bound gives 0 < |V| < 0.40825 M. Immediate. For M an odd prime this is the hypothesis O.7 already uses; squarefree costs nothing extra. Verified over realised in-window pairs at X = 3000 and 6000, together with gcd(a,M) = 1 (0 classes violate it), which is what the step p | A_V - B_V = 2Va => p | V needs.
claims.notes: The whole content is that |V| < M turns 'p does not divide V for some p' from a hypothesis into a pigeonhole, and squarefreeness is exactly what makes rad(M) = M. Measured coverage of realised close pairs at X = 6000: odd prime 90/751 = 12.0%, odd squarefree 128/751 = 17.0%, so the extension takes O.7 from 12.0% to 29.0%. Odd non-squarefree is a further 10.3% and satisfied the hypothesis on 77/77, but is NOT free -- rad(M) can sit far below the |V| ceiling -- so it is measured, not proved. Even M is 60.7% and is out of reach of this route entirely, since p | 2Va => p | V needs p odd. Superseded in the same way as the M_1 claim: the valuation form needs no hypothesis on M at all, so the hypotheses this claim weakens or proves are no longer on the path. Kept as true; not live.

claims.statement: Theorem O.8 assumes gcd(V,M) = 1 on each of the three pairwise steps. That is SUFFICIENT but not necessary: the three-moduli contradiction can be run at a SINGLE prime p | M, needing only p not dividing V_12, V_23 and V_13. At such a p the local subcase (whether p | S or p | T) is defined and flips at every step, so xi_1 -> xi_2 -> xi_3 returns it while xi_1 -> xi_3 flips it, and one prime suffices for the contradiction -- the whole pair (gcd(M,S), gcd(M,T)) need not swap. So the minimal hypothesis is 'some p | M divides none of the three V', which is strictly weaker than gcd(V,M) = 1.
claims.notes: What the pigeonhole buys and what it does not. PER STEP the hypothesis is FREE for M odd squarefree: if every p | M divided V then M = rad(M) | V, against 0 < |V| < M. So the dichotomy is unconditional at some prime for each step separately. It does NOT give the three-step version, because the pigeonhole can return a DIFFERENT prime for each of the three steps, and three proper subsets of the primes of M can cover them all. Making the bad sets empty -- gcd(V,M) = 1 -- is one way to force a common prime and is what O.8 assumes; requiring a common prime is another and is weaker. Empirically they do not separate: every in-window pair with M odd has gcd(V,M) = 1 (their 295/295 at X = 6000), so no realised configuration distinguishes the two hypotheses, and the weaker one is worth stating only because it is what a proof would actually have to supply. INFERRED: I derived the single-prime reduction from their statement of the argument, and have not re-derived Proposition O.6's flip at a single prime rather than mod M, which is the step that would make it real. Superseded in the same way as the M_1 claim: the valuation form needs no hypothesis on M at all, so the hypotheses this claim weakens or proves are no longer on the path. Kept as true; not live.

claims.statement: For any shared modulus m of the class (a,b), with S = X+Y and T = X-Y: S*T = -M*m. Proof: aY^2 - bX^2 = M with b = a+M gives a(Y^2 - X^2) = M(X^2+1) = M a m. Consequently, for M odd, gcd(M,S)*gcd(M,T) = M: with p^e || M, v_p(S) + v_p(T) = e + v_p(m); if p divides both S and T then p | X, so am = X^2+1 == 1 mod p and p nmid m, leaving v_p(S) + v_p(T) = e with both terms <= e.
claims.notes: 0 failures over 822,349 solutions at X = 4000 for both the identity and the factorisation, and the p|S, p|T => p|X => p nmid m step checked on all 141,277 instances. This turns O.7's dichotomy into a FACTORISATION M = M+ M- with M+ | S and M- | T, which is what lets the argument localise to composite M.

claims.statement: Theorem O.8. For M odd and SQUAREFREE, if gcd(V,M) = 1 on each of the three pairwise steps, no dyadic window contains three shared moduli. Squarefreeness makes gcd(M,S) gcd(M,T) = M a dichotomy per prime; gcd(V,M) = 1 makes the local sign defined at every p | M, so the local subcase flips at each prime and the pair (gcd(M,S), gcd(M,T)) SWAPS. Two steps restore it, one step swaps it, and M+ = M- is impossible for M squarefree > 1. Extends Theorem O.7 from M odd prime to M odd squarefree, at the cost of one hypothesis.
claims.notes: SUPERSEDED BY theorem-O9-pigeonhole, which reaches the same conclusion with NO hypothesis: the coprimality gcd(V,M) = 1 was not needed. Kept because the factorisation lemma it rests on is used by O.9, and because the conditional form was the step that made the unconditional one findable. THE HYPOTHESIS IS OBSERVED, NOT PROVED, and that is the gap. Every in-window pair with M odd has gcd(V,M) = 1 -- 295 of 295 at X = 6000, 197 of 197 at X = 4000 -- but the window bound |V| < 0.57735 M/sqrt(D) bounds V without making it coprime to M. gcd(V,M) = 1 is EQUIVALENT to g = gcd(U,V) = 1 (g | M and g | V give g | gcd(V,M); conversely p | gcd(V,M) forces p | U since U^2 = M^2 + D V^2), so it is the same quantity Prop O.1's chain tracks, where all that is known in-window is a g^2 < M, which permits g > 1. TWO CONDITIONS, NOT ONE: coprimality is what separates swap from non-swap (every non-swap has gcd(V,M) > 1; none among 1333 coprime pairs), while squarefreeness is needed so the split is a dichotomy rather than partial -- M = 9 gives (3,3), neither p^e | S nor p^e | T. A first pass recorded the non-swaps as 'all at M = 9' from an example list; the distribution is M = 3, 9, 11, 15, 21, 23, mostly squarefree. M EVEN remains outside everything here: a, b both odd makes M and V both even, so gcd(V,M) >= 2 automatically.

claims.statement: For M odd squarefree, p | M, gcd(a,M) = 1: p | V if and only if the two moduli sit in the SAME local subcase at p. Proof: a(Y^2 - X^2) = 0 mod p forces p | S or p | T; not both, since p | S and p | T give p | X, hence am = X^2+1 = 1 mod p and p does not divide m, and then S T = -M m forces v_p(S) + v_p(T) = 1 while both positive makes it >= 2. So exactly one holds and p does not divide X. Writing Y = eps X mod p with eps = -1 on p | S and +1 on p | T, V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i = X_i X_j (eps_j - eps_i) mod p: zero when the subcases agree, +-2 X_i X_j and nonzero when they differ. Verified: 949 (a,b,p) instances at X = 3000, 0 violations, both directions exercised (30 agree-and-divide, 919 differ-and-not), and p | X occurred 0 times.
claims.notes: Collapses two things that were being carried separately. Proposition O.6's alternation and Theorem O.8's gcd(V,M) = 1 hypothesis are the SAME statement: the subcase flips at a step precisely when p does not divide that step's V. So O.6 is not independent evidence for O.8 -- it is O.8's hypothesis, observed on the pairs where it can be observed. Built on the parallel session's S T = -M m, which is what makes the not-both step work.

claims.statement: Theorem O.8's hypothesis can be cut from three pairwise steps to two consecutive ones. If gcd(V_12, M) = gcd(V_23, M) = 1 with M odd squarefree, then by the subcase equivalence the local subcase differs across 1-2 and across 2-3, hence AGREES across 1-3, hence every p | M divides V_13, hence M | V_13 since M is squarefree -- contradicting 0 < |V_13| < 0.40825 M from the in-window bound. So no dyadic window holds three shared moduli, and nothing need be assumed about V_13.
claims.notes: A third of the hypothesis comes off, and the shape of what remains is clearer: the open question is entirely whether gcd(V,M) = 1 holds on in-window pairs, which is a statement about PAIRS -- realised, 295 of 295 at X = 6000 -- and no longer about triples, which are not realised and so cannot be swept for at all. That is the distinction the parallel session drew about O.7's measurability, arriving one level down: the hypothesis is now entirely on the observable side of it. SUBSUMED by the parallel session's Theorem O.9, which takes the same sign equivalence and needs no hypothesis at all: three signs in {+-1} cannot be pairwise distinct, so every p | M divides one of V_12, V_23, V_13 and M | V_12 V_23 V_13 for M squarefree, and the window bound then forces 3ab < M^{4/3}. My version cut the hypothesis from three steps to two; theirs removes it. Kept as true and not refuted, but it is not the live statement -- the live one is O.9.

claims.statement: Note O recorded 'the triple question has a proved unconditional constraint M/sqrt(D) >= 11.484, which is the parallel session's Plucker-parity argument'. The DERIVATION does not give that value and the constraint is not unconditional. With the exact |V| < (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R), R = X_k/X_i, the stated argument (|V_ik| >= 4, R < sqrt2) gives 8 sqrt2 = 11.3137; and R < sqrt2 is only the asymptotic window condition, the exact one being R^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2, which at X_i = 1 gives just 6.93.
claims.notes: Kept so it cannot be silently re-asserted. THE VALUE 11.484 IS CORRECT -- Theorem O.4 proves it by composition, where 2^(1/4) enters from the composite tau_1^2 < sqrt2 rather than from |V| >= 4 -- and the two expressions are algebraically identical: 4/(2^(1/4) - 2^(-1/4)) = 4(2^(1/4) + 2^(3/4)) = 11.48400. So this is a right answer with a wrong route attached, which is harder to catch than a wrong answer and was found only by deriving the same constant independently and asking why they agreed.

claims.statement: V * W = M * (m_i - m_j), where V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i and W = X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j. Proof: V W = X_i^2 Y_j^2 - X_j^2 Y_i^2, and Y^2 = X^2 + M m turns that into M(X_i^2 m_j - X_j^2 m_i), which with m = (X^2+1)/a is M(X_i^2 - X_j^2)/a = M(m_i - m_j) since X^2 = a m - 1. The cofactor a cancels entirely. 0 failures over 964 consecutive pairs with M odd at X = 4000. Consequences: for M odd squarefree, exactly one of V, W is divisible by each p | M, so gcd(V,M) = 1 if and only if M | W -- verified 0 failures over 744 pairs -- and the valuations are exact: v_p(V) = 1 + v_p(m_i - m_j) when the subcases agree, v_p(W) = 1 + v_p(m_i - m_j) when they differ (30 and 919 instances at X = 3000, 0 failures).
claims.notes: The cleanest form the O.8 hypothesis has taken: it is the single divisibility M | W. M | W holds 197/197 in-window at X = 4000 and only 680/767 = 88.7% out of window, so the window is doing real work rather than the divisibility being automatic. NOT proved, and the size argument does not reach it: |V| < 0.57735 M/sqrt(D), so gcd(V,M) > 1 is excluded by size only when every prime of M exceeds 0.57735 M/sqrt(D). At a = 1 that reads p > 0.577 sqrt(M), which fails for M = 33 among others -- so classes exist where nothing but the arithmetic forbids it.

claims.statement: Theorem O.9. For M = b-a odd and squarefree, a dyadic window contains three shared moduli (with X_1 >= 1) only if 3ab < (b-a)^{4/3} -- equivalently a < (t-1)^2/(3t)^{3/2} for t = b/a, so asymptotically b > 27 a^3. Proof: for p | M, aY^2 = bX^2 + M gives Y^2 == X^2 mod p and p nmid X (else p | Y so p | S and p | T, while S T = -M m with v_p(M) = 1 forces v_p(S) + v_p(T) = 1), so each solution carries a sign sigma = +-1 with Y == sigma X. Then V_ij == X_i X_j (sigma_j - sigma_i) mod p, so p | V_ij iff sigma_i = sigma_j. Three signs in {+-1} cannot be pairwise distinct, so every p | M divides one of V_12, V_23, V_13; for M squarefree that is M | V_12 V_23 V_13. In a window |V| < M/sqrt(3D), so M <= |product| < M^3/(3D)^{3/2}. Recovers Theorem O.7 for M prime with NO hypothesis, and supersedes O.8's coprimality assumption.
claims.notes: SUPERSEDED BY theorem-O10-valuation, which drops the odd and squarefree hypotheses entirely by replacing the two-valued sign with a valuation split s + t >= e. Kept because the sign is the e = 1 shadow of that and is how the argument was found. NOT A WEAK CONDITION: at X = 4000, 499,188 of 503,054 classes with M odd squarefree (99.2%) fail 3ab < M^{4/3} and are excluded outright. With O.4's t > 133.875 the admissible a is tiny -- a <= 2 at the minimum admissible t, 6 at t = 1e3, 19 at t = 1e4. Verified at X = 4000: 0 failures over 1,588,226 sign determinations and 1317 (p,pair) equivalence checks; 0 failures of M | V12 V23 V13 over the realised triples; 0 failures of |V| < M/sqrt(3D) over 139 in-window pairs. THE CLEANER IDENTITY IS THE PARALLEL SESSION'S: V W = M (m_i - m_j) with W = X_j Y_i + X_i Y_j -- mine divided by a, and the cofactor cancels entirely (0 failures over 2747 pairs). It also gives gcd(V,M) = 1 <=> M | W for M odd squarefree. STILL OPEN: M even and M non-squarefree, where sigma is undefined -- at M = 9 the pair (gcd(M,S), gcd(M,T)) is (3,3) and p | X becomes possible.

claims.statement: For M = b - a odd, V = X_i Y_j - X_j Y_i is always even. M odd means a and b are not both 2 mod 4. If a and b are both odd then m must be odd -- m even would give am and bm even, so X and Y both odd, so a = b = 2 mod 4 is not needed but M = b-a even, a contradiction -- and then X^2 = am-1 and Y^2 = bm-1 are both even, so X and Y are both even. If a = 2 mod 4 and b is odd then m is odd, X^2 = am-1 is odd and Y^2 = bm-1 is even, so X is odd and Y even. Either way every term of V has an even factor. Verified over all consecutive pairs at X = 4000: 0 odd |V| out of 2566.
claims.notes: Small and load-bearing: it turns |V| < 4 into |V| = 2, which is what makes the Plucker threshold prove O.8's hypothesis rather than merely bound V. SCOPE MEASURED: the lemma is stated and proved for x^2+1, and it does NOT generalise. At X = 1500 over classes with M odd, |V| is even for D = 1,2,3,4,5,6,11,19,29 and ODD in 192 of 1018 pairs at D = 7 and 608 of 2222 at D = 39. The proof uses x^2+1's mod-4 structure specifically, so this is a confirmation of the scope rather than a surprise -- but it matters, because every |V| >= 2 threshold in the D analysis is conditional on it, and D = 7 and D = 39 are outside.

claims.statement: O.8's hypothesis gcd(V,M) = 1 is a THEOREM, not an observation, whenever M/sqrt(D) <= 8/(sqrt r - 1/sqrt r) with r = 2 + 1/X_i^2 -- i.e. 4 sqrt 3 = 6.9282 at X_i = 1, rising to 8 sqrt 2 = 11.3137. Chain, all proved: the bound |V| < (M/2 sqrt D)(sqrt r - 1/sqrt r) from V W = M(m_i - m_j) and Y > X sqrt(b/a); V even for M odd; V nonzero. So below the threshold |V| < 4 forces |V| = 2, and gcd(2,M) = 1. Coverage at X = 4000: 234 of 498 in-window pairs (47.0%) are below the threshold and ALL have |V| = 2; 95 of those have M odd and all have gcd(V,M) = 1 by the argument rather than by measurement.
claims.notes: The Plucker bound and O.8's hypothesis turn out to be the same inequality read in opposite directions. The parallel session had just corrected the bound's derivation -- it gives 8 sqrt 2, not 11.484 -- and treated it as a constraint on TRIPLES; used as a constraint on a single step it proves the pair-level hypothesis outright below the threshold. Above it, |V| >= 4 becomes possible and the hypothesis is open: measured 0 counterexamples over 295 in-window M-odd pairs at X = 6000 and 451 at X = 9000, and the only in-window pairs with |V| > 2 anywhere in the data -- |V| = 24, 66, 182 at (53,423125), (1,51701), (1,423125) -- all have M EVEN, hence gcd(V,M) >= 2 automatically and nothing to prove. Superseded in the same way as the M_1 claim: the valuation form needs no hypothesis on M at all, so the hypotheses this claim weakens or proves are no longer on the path. Kept as true; not live.

claims.statement: Theorem O.9 generalises off M odd squarefree and reaches M EVEN. Nothing in the sign argument is about M -- it is about a single odd prime p with p || M, which is what makes the sign well defined (p | S and p | T would give p | X, and S T = -M m with v_p(M) = 1 forces v_p(S) + v_p(T) = 1). Let M_1 = product of the odd primes p with p || M. Each such p divides one of V_12, V_23, V_13 since three signs in {+-1} cannot be pairwise distinct; M_1 is squarefree, so M_1 | V_12 V_23 V_13; and |V| < M/sqrt(3D) gives M_1 < M^3/(3D)^{3/2}. Hence a dyadic window holds three shared moduli only if 3ab < (M^3/M_1)^{2/3}. For M odd squarefree M_1 = M and this is O.9's 3ab < M^{4/3}. Coverage, on the only population where the statement is not vacuous -- classes with at least 3 shared moduli, since fewer than 3 cannot host a triple whatever any theorem says: at X = 3000 there are 60 such classes out of 1,815,154, and the bound excludes 9 (15.0%), leaves 30 admissible (50.0%), and is silent on 21 (35.0%, M_1 = 1). Restricted further to M odd squarefree, where the bound is O.9's own 3ab < M^{4/3}, it excludes 6 of 11. Zero classes have three moduli in one dyadic window at this X.
claims.notes: The hypothesis 'M odd squarefree' was doing two jobs and only one of them was needed. Squarefreeness of M is used nowhere: what is used is v_p(M) = 1 at the single prime being worked at, and M_1 collects exactly those primes. Oddness of M is not needed either -- only oddness of p. Verified on M EVEN specifically, which is the new range: sign well defined, p never divides X, and p | V iff the signs agree, over 200+ (pair, p) instances at X = 2000. The conclusion is a configuration that does not occur, so only the hypotheses are checkable; they are checked on pairs, which do occur. COVERAGE FIGURES CORRECTED, and the first version was the repo's own trap. I reported '95.68% of classes excluded outright, silent on 1.02%' over ALL 1,815,154 classes -- of which 1,815,094 have FEWER THAN 3 MODULI and cannot host a triple regardless. So 99.997% of that denominator was vacuous and both figures were meaningless as stated. On the 60 classes that could host one, the bound excludes 15% and is silent on 35%. The rule this repo already carries -- the informative subset is never the one the loop naturally counts -- and I wrote a sweep over every class because every class is what ratio_classes returns. The THEOREM is unaffected; only its advertised reach was. SUPERSEDED by the parallel session's p-adic valuation form, which drops every hypothesis on M rather than weakening one: s_i = min(e, v_p(S_i)), t_i = min(e, v_p(T_i)), s_i + t_i >= e, and ordering by s gives M | V_12 V_13 V_23 with no M_1 and no restriction to v_p(M) = 1. My version reached the same conclusion on the primes that exactly divide M; theirs reaches it on all of them, because when p | X the split simply puts weight on both s and t and the ordering still works. Kept as true and correctly derived, but it is not the live statement. The sequence -- their M odd squarefree, my odd p || M, their full valuation form -- is three passes at the same argument, each removing a hypothesis the previous one had thought structural.

claims.statement: Theorem O.10. For ANY M = b-a -- odd or even, squarefree or not -- M | V_12 V_23 V_13 for three shared moduli of a class; hence, since a dyadic window gives 0 < |V| < M/sqrt(3D), a window holds three only if 3ab < (b-a)^{4/3}. Proof: gcd(a,M) = 1, and for p^e || M, b == a mod p^e with aY^2 = bX^2 + M gives Y^2 == X^2 mod p^e, i.e. p^e | S T (Lemma S T = -M m). With s_i = min(e, v_p(S_i)) and t_i = min(e, v_p(T_i)) we get s_i + t_i >= e; p^{s_i} | S_i gives Y_i == -X_i mod p^{s_i} and p^{t_i} | T_i gives Y_i == X_i mod p^{t_i}, either of which kills V_ij, so v_p(V_ij) >= max(min(s_i,s_j), min(t_i,t_j)). Ordering s_1 <= s_2 <= s_3 gives v_p(V_23) >= s_2 and v_p(V_12) >= e - s_2, so their sum is >= e.
claims.notes: SHARPENED BY theorem-O11-coupled-ratios, which uses R_12 R_23 = R_13 to replace the constant 1/3 by 0.048628 -- 6.85x -- and lifts the informative coverage from ~35% to 88-98%. O.10's divisibility M | V12 V23 V13 is what O.11 rests on. THE SIGN IS THE e = 1 SHADOW: at v_p(M) = 1, S T = -M m forces s + t = 1 exactly, so (s,t) is (1,0) or (0,1), which is sigma = -+1. 'Three signs in {+-1} collide' becomes 'order by s and take the middle two', and that is the only step that changes. NO CASE REMAINS: O.9 needed M odd squarefree and the parallel session's intermediate M_1 = prod{odd p || M} form left 1.02% of classes silent (M a power of two times a powerful odd part); the valuation form covers those and excludes 99.2% of them. COVERAGE, WITH ITS DENOMINATOR. A first version reported '99.26% of classes excluded', which is over EVERY ratio class -- and a class with fewer than three shared moduli cannot host a triple at all. At X = 3000 only 60 of 1,815,154 classes have three shared moduli, so that figure measured vacuity, not reach. On the INFORMATIVE population it is ~35% and stable: 17/48 (35.4%) at X = 2000, 21/60 (35.0%) at 3000, 24/70 (34.3%) at 4000, 34/96 (35.4%) at 6000. The gain over the M_1 form survives: on the same 60 classes it excludes 21 with none silent, against 9 excluded and 21 silent. Found by the parallel session in its own figures and applying identically here. Verified 0 failures at X = 4000 over 12,447,219 checks of s + t >= e, 6266 of the v_p(V) bound, 224 of the ordered two-term sum, and M | V12 V23 V13 on every realised triple in all categories (odd squarefree 23, odd non-squarefree 39, even non-squarefree 216).

claims.statement: The sign argument needs an odd p | M, so it is silent on M a pure power of two, and those classes are the modulus-rich ones. Share of classes with M = 2^e: at X = 3000, 0.013% of all classes, 8.3% of classes with >= 3 shared moduli, 16.7% with >= 4, 50.0% with >= 5; at X = 6000, 0.004%, 6.2%, 15.4%, 33.3%. A 600x to 4000x enrichment, stable across a doubling of X. The single richest class in the data -- (1,5), M = 4, eight shared moduli 2, 10, 65, 442, 3026, 20737, 142130, 974170 -- is one, and so are (1,17) and (1,65): these are b = 2^e + 1 with a = 1, the Pell chains.
claims.notes: The reason the reach figures needed correcting twice. By class count the blind spot is negligible; on the population that could host a triple it is 35%, and among the richest classes it is half. So it is not a uniform residue to be mopped up later -- it is concentrated on exactly the configurations where a counterexample would live, and the correlation is not weak. Recorded as `rigorous_finite` at two sizes rather than extrapolated: the enrichment is stable but no law is fitted to it, and the counts at >= 5 moduli are 6 and 9, which is too few to fit anything to. SUPERSEDED IN SIGNIFICANCE, though the measurement stands. The parallel session's p-adic valuation form of the sign argument drops every hypothesis on M -- s_i = min(e, v_p(S_i)), t_i = min(e, v_p(T_i)), s_i + t_i >= e, and ordering by s gives the two needed terms -- so the silent class is CLOSED, not merely reduced, and goes from 35.0% of informative classes to 0. The enrichment figures remain true as facts about where M = 2^e and M_1 = 1 sit in the population; what is no longer true is the reading that they mark where the remaining work is. They do not: the remaining work is the 39 of 60 informative classes that are ADMISSIBLE under 3ab < M^{4/3} and hold no triple anyway.

claims.statement: The valuation argument's per-prime conclusion v_p(V_12) + v_p(V_23) >= e does NOT give M | V_12 V_23 for any fixed pair, because the s-ordering that selects the pair is computed per prime and different primes select different pairs. Only the three-term product is uniform: M | V_12 V_13 V_23. Counterexamples exist: 5 of 216 realised triples at X = 3000 admit NO single pair whose product is divisible by M -- (1,481) M=480 moduli 2,1157,17690; (1,925) M=924 moduli 2,5,7922; (1,106) M=105 moduli 5,65,4097; (1,2465) M=2464 moduli 10,37,530; (1,1450) M=1449 moduli 17,65,901 -- all with M carrying three or more distinct primes. The per-prime statement itself holds: 216 of 216 triples, 0 failures.
claims.notes: Recorded because the two-term version would CLOSE Conjecture O.2 outright and it is the obvious next move. If M | V_a V_b for a fixed in-window pair, then M <= |V_a V_b| < M^2/(3D) gives 3ab < M = b - a, which is impossible for a >= 1 since 3ab >= 3b > b - a. I derived exactly that and was one step from asserting the conjecture proved. The quantifier is what fails: the pair depends on p. The three-term product gives only 3ab < M^{4/3}, which is satisfiable. This is the 'right answer with a wrong route' shape caught before the assertion rather than after -- and it was caught by asking which objects the quantifier ranges over, not by any number coming out wrong, since every number in the per-prime check was correct.

claims.statement: Theorem O.11. Since R_12 R_23 = R_13, the three per-pair bounds |V_ij| < (M/sqrt D) sinh(u_ij) cannot all sit at the window's edge. For fixed u_13, sinh(u_12) sinh(u_23) is maximised at the equal split u_12 = u_23 = u_13/2 (derivative sinh(u_13 - 2u_12)), so f(R_12) f(R_23) f(R_13) <= 16 sinh^3(u/2) cosh(u/2) = (sqrt rho - 1/sqrt rho)^3 (sqrt rho + 1/sqrt rho) =: C(X_1) with rho = sqrt(2 + 1/X_1^2). With M <= |V12 V23 V13| that gives ab < (C(X_1)/8)^{2/3} (b-a)^{4/3}: 0.125873 at X_1 = 1 falling to 0.048628 asymptotically, against O.10's 1/3 -- 6.85x stronger.
claims.notes: COVERAGE, WITH ITS POPULATION AND ITS TREND. Over classes with >= 3 shared moduli -- the only ones that could host a triple -- O.11 excludes 42/43, 46/48, 57/60, 65/70, 88/96, 96/109 at X = 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000, i.e. 97.7%, 95.8%, 95.0%, 92.9%, 91.7%, 88.1%. DO NOT READ THAT AS AN ASYMPTOTIC: O.10's ~35% is flat in X while O.11's falls monotonically, and the admissible count roughly doubles as X doubles (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13) while the informative population grows only 2.5x over that range. The reach may tend to 0 and no claim is made about its limit. The equal-split maximisation was confirmed numerically to eight digits over a 4000-point grid at four values of w.

claims.statement: Theorem O.11's constant, re-derived and cross-checked. With R_ij = e^{u_ij} the bound |V_ij| < (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R) is |V_ij| < (M/sqrt D) sinh(u_ij), and R_12 R_23 = R_13 means u_12 + u_23 = u_13, so sinh(u_12) sinh(u_23) is maximised at the equal split -- the derivative is sinh(u_13 - 2 u_12), zero exactly at u_12 = u_13/2 and changing sign there. Hence the triple product is < (M/sqrt D)^3 * 2 sinh^3(u/2) cosh(u/2) = (M/sqrt D)^3 K/8 with K = (sqrt rho - 1/sqrt rho)^3 (sqrt rho + 1/sqrt rho), rho = sqrt(2 + 1/X_1^2). M <= product then gives ab < (K/8)^{2/3} M^{4/3}. Computed: K/8^{2/3} = 0.125873 at X_1 = 1, 0.049344 at X_1 = 10, 0.048628 asymptotically; against O.10's 1/3 that is 6.855x. The sinh form and the sqrt-rho form agree to 6 places (0.010723 both).
claims.notes: Verified by re-deriving rather than re-running. The step worth checking was the maximisation, since 'all three R at the window edge' is exactly the over-count O.10 makes and the constraint R_12 R_23 = R_13 is what forbids it; the derivative sinh(u_13 - 2u_12) is clean and the equal split is a genuine maximum. I got 0.1421 on the first pass by using 0.5946 for 2^{1/4} - 2^{-1/4} instead of 0.34831 -- their number is right and mine was an arithmetic slip. Their trend caveat is the important half: the reach 97.7 -> 88.1% is FALLING over X = 1500 to 8000 with the admissible count doubling per doubling of X, so no limit is claimed and none should be.

claims.statement: `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows` and Note O's Conjecture O.2 are the same statement. The off-diagonal Gram entry of the rational graph restricted to a dyadic window [N,2N) is the number of moduli in that window shared by a cofactor pair (a,b); O.2 says no dyadic window contains three shared moduli. So 'max windowed Gram entry is 2' IS 'no window holds three', with no translation. Verified directly: max shared moduli in one dyadic window is 2 at X = 2000 and 4000, attained at (1,41) with moduli 730 and 1370, and zero classes hold three.
claims.notes: This is why the Note O thread is not a side quest. `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows` is `rigorous_finite` -- 'uniformly for X <= 8000' -- and it is what Note L's conclusion rests on, that merging rows over Z thickens each side separately and never jointly. Theorems O.9 and O.11 prove exactly that bound on the classes satisfying 3ab < M^{4/3} and its sharpened form, so the Note O work is PROMOTING a central finite measurement of Note L toward a theorem for all X. NOT NEW, and my commit message claiming 'neither note said so' was false. Note L's section 'What proving the triple statement would actually buy' states it outright -- "'No dyadic window holds three' is exactly G'(n1,n2) restricted to a window <= 2" -- and says it would move `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows` from rigorous_finite to proved. I wrote that section. I re-derived it, asserted it was a connection neither note had drawn, and sent it to the parallel session as new. The identification stands; the novelty did not. AND NOTE L IS MORE CAREFUL THAN THIS CLAIM WAS. It adds that proving it upgrades one claim's STATUS and changes no conclusion -- the argument uses only that there is no main term to extract, and a bounded count supplies none at 1, 2 or 3 alike -- and it warns that the O.2 work 'reads, from the volume of it, like something with more at stake'. The parallel session's `triple-question-upgrades-status-not-conclusion` matches Note L exactly, and my message to them calling this 'a stronger framing than upgrades-status-not-conclusion' had it backwards: theirs was the careful reading and mine was the inflated one. Partial, not complete: O.11's measured reach is falling with X, so what is proved is a shrinking share of the classes, and the promotion is not yet available. The identification is definitional -- it is about what the two statements SAY -- so it does not depend on the measurement, and the dependency guard rejected the edge I first wrote to `rational-gram-bounded-on-windows`. That is the third time tonight it has caught the same habit: listing the neighbouring result as a premise because it is the thing the claim is ABOUT. A claim about X is not a claim resting on X, and the ordering rule is what keeps the two apart.

claims.statement: Every ratio class that Theorem O.11 admits, among those holding >= 3 shared moduli, has a = 1. Across X = 1500, 2000, 3000, 4000, 6000, 8000 there are 9, 12, 16, 19, 30, 33 informative classes with a >= 2 -- 119 in total -- and O.11 excludes EVERY one, while the a = 1 admitted counts are 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. This matters because full-graph-growth-is-pell records that n1 = 1 cannot occur in a Type II hypothesis, where both variables are confined to ranges: so on the classes the Type II question actually ranges over, O.11 is currently exhaustive.
claims.notes: A RANGE EFFECT, NOT A LAW, and the law is easy to write down: O.11 admits (a,b) as soon as ab < c (b-a)^{4/3}, and for FIXED a the right side wins as b -> infinity. The crossover is b ~ 9.0e3 at a = 1, 7.0e4 at a = 2, 2.4e5 at a = 3, 1.1e6 at a = 5. So the a >= 2 column is empty because the sweep does not reach far enough in b, and it WILL fill in at larger X -- the a = 1 column is already filling. Recorded with the crossover values precisely so the finite reading cannot be mistaken for a structural one; this is the same failure the denominator correction was about, anticipated rather than repaired.

claims.statement: That O.11 excludes every informative class with a >= 2 is a RANGE effect and not a structural fact, confirmed independently. O.11 admits (a,b) once ab < 0.048628 (b-a)^{4/3}, so for fixed a the right side wins as b grows; crossover b is ~9e3 at a = 1, ~7e4 at a = 2, ~2.37e5 at a = 3, ~1.13e6 at a = 5 -- reproduced to the digits given. But the largest b among informative classes with a >= 2 is 925 at X = 3000 and 8321 at X = 6000, an order of magnitude below the a = 2 crossover. So the a >= 2 column is empty because the sweep cannot reach it, and the data cannot test the question at all. The single admissible class at X = 6000 is (1, 18241), which sits above the a = 1 crossover exactly as predicted.
claims.notes: Worth keeping because of how it was caught rather than what it says. A column of zeros that is going to fill looks identical to a column of zeros that is a law, and neither the population check nor the >90% check separates them -- only the direction of travel does, which is the third layer of the percentage rule and the one the parallel session added. They anticipated the failure and recorded the crossover values inside the claim so the finite reading cannot be mistaken for a structural one; I confirmed the crossovers and then measured the largest b actually available, which is the part that settles it. Note the near-miss underneath: a = 1 means the unit cofactor, which no Type II hypothesis admits, so 'O.11 is exhaustive on the classes Type II ranges over' was available as a headline and would have been false for range reasons alone.

claims.statement: Theorem O.12. If n_2/n_1 < (5+sqrt21)/2 = 4.7913 -- in particular if n_1 and n_2 lie in ONE DYADIC BAND -- then they share at most one modulus in any dyadic window. So the rational incidence graph restricted to the doubly-dyadic configuration (cofactors banded, moduli windowed) is C_4-FREE. Proof: a pair of shared moduli m_i < m_j < 2 m_i with X_i >= 1 needs tau_V^2 < 2 + 1/X_i^2 <= 3; tau increases in |V| and |V| >= 1, so tau_V >= tau(1) = sqrt(1+s^2) + s with s = sqrt(D)/M, and tau(1)^2 < 3 forces M/sqrt(D) > sqrt3. With u = n_2/n_1 = b/a, M/sqrt(D) = (u-1)/sqrt(u), and that exceeds sqrt3 iff u^2 - 5u + 1 > 0 iff u > (5+sqrt21)/2. A dyadic band gives u < 2, a factor 2.4 inside.
claims.notes: VERIFIED AT SCALE WITH THE CORRECTED CRITERION. The earlier measurements here used dyadic windows ANCHORED at powers of two (and of four), which is strictly weaker than the statement -- [8,16) and [16,32) between them miss the pair (9,17). Redone testing by RATIO on both axes at X = 2500: 1,404,197 banded cofactor pairs share a modulus, ALL of them share exactly one, and ZERO share two; max Gram banded 1, free 2, with 426 free pairs sharing two as the positive control. The theorem was never in doubt -- it is proved -- but its verification had been testing a weaker proposition than the one it is named for, which is a third variety of guard failure beyond the two catalogued (a guard that cannot fail, and one that covers nothing). It was caught by two sessions' sweeps disagreeing about c = 6, not by any check. WHY IT MATTERS OUTSIDE NOTE O. gaussian-to-rational-bridge is `inferred` and its stated gap is 'what is proved over Z[i] is G <= 1; what is measured over Z is G' <= 2 on every dyadic window for X <= 8000'. Ford-Maynard's (II) has ARBITRARY divisor-bounded coefficients, so it implies its own doubly-banded restriction, and footnote 2's quantity is doubly banded outright -- its pair by their own 'm1,m2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}' and its shared variable by their own J subset (x/2,x], which forces a ratio-2 range. (Their (II) sums over (x/2)^theta < m <= x^{theta+nu}, NOT a band when nu > 0; the coefficients supply the banding, not the range -- see fm-configuration-is-doubly-banded-at-source.) So BOTH variables are banded -- fm-barrier-range-is-small-moduli records that footnote 2 averages over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}. On that configuration O.12 proves G' <= 1 over Z for all X, matching the Z[i] bound exactly rather than being a measured constant one larger. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE: the bridge's remaining inference, 'both give no main term, so the conclusion is unchanged', is untouched -- O.12 removes the quantitative discrepancy and the finite floor, not the reasoning. And it says nothing about O.2, the free-cofactor question: (1,41) shares 730 and 1370, a genuine G' = 2, with 41/1 = 41 far outside one band. Measured at X = 2000, 3000 and 6000: banded max Gram 1 at every dyadic modulus window, free max Gram 2. Uses |V| >= 1 rather than the parity lemma's |V| >= 2, so it is independent of the parity of a and b. POSITIVE CONTROL, since a 'max of 1' over pairs that share nothing would look identical and mean nothing: at X = 3000 over 300,026 banded cofactor pairs, 57,132 share exactly one modulus and 0 share two or more, while 127 FREE pairs share two. The forbidden configuration occurs the moment the banding is dropped, so the sweep is not vacuous and the hypothesis is what is doing the work. NOT KNIFE-EDGE: the proved threshold 4.7913 uses only |V| >= 1; with |V| >= 2 (the parity lemma, whenever M is odd) it rises to 13.9282 at X_1 = 1 and 33.9706 asymptotically. Empirically the minimum n_2/n_1 among pairs sharing two moduli in one window is 43.79 at (34,1489) with moduli 1073 and 1973, over 125 such pairs at X = 3000 -- 9.1x the proved bound. So the theorem covers any reasonable reading of 'both variables in ranges', not only the dyadic one. CORRECTED: the minimum quoted here as 43.79 at (34,1489) with moduli 1073 and 1973 is NOT the minimum. It is 34.0811 at (37,1261) with moduli 866 and 1730, which is reachable at X = 3000. The 43.79 came from an ANCHORED-window sweep: 866 and 1730 have ratio 1.9977 and lie in one dyadic window by ratio, but a doubling sweep puts them in [512,1024) and [1024,2048) and never compares them, while 1073 and 1973 both sit inside [1024,2048). So '9.1x the proved bound' is 7.11x. The theorem itself is untouched -- max Gram 1 on banded cofactors is proved, not measured. See O12-is-loose-by-a-factor-seven.

claims.statement: Note K's line result and Note L's degree ladder are the same fact seen from the two sides. N(a+ci) = a^2 + c^2, so a LINE in Z[i] is a degree-2 single-variable sequence over Z; Note L's ladder gives kappa = X^{2-d}, hence kappa = 1 exactly at d = 2, and Note K gives kappa = 1 - c^2/Q -> 1 for every line. The geometry is the explanation of the exponent: a line's count is its length, and its length is sqrt(Q). On the Z side the family is uniform too -- with windows normalised to each sequence's own sqrt(Q), the max off-diagonal Gram excluding the unit modulus is 2 at [sqrt Q, 2 sqrt Q) and [sqrt Q/2, sqrt Q) for every c = 1,2,3,5,7,11,13 at X = 3000, with occasional 3s only at sqrt(Q)/8 and below.
claims.notes: NORMALISATION TRAP, recorded because I nearly published the opposite. Measured on FIXED windows [64,256) the same quantity reads 2,3,3,3,4,5,6 across c = 1..13, which says the Z-vs-Z[i] gap widens with c and that x^2+1 is unusually tight -- an attractive finding and false. A fixed window sits at a different depth in each sequence's value range, since x^2+c^2 starts at 1+c^2; normalising the window to each sequence's own sqrt(Q) removes the effect almost entirely. The repo's normalisation rule already says to state which quantity an exponent is relative to; this is the same rule for a WINDOW, across sequences, where it is easier to miss because the window looks like an absolute range.

claims.statement: The C4-free obstruction holds in BOTH formulations on the configuration a Type II hypothesis quantifies over, so it does not depend on the choice of ring. Note F proves G <= 1 over Z[i] for all cofactor pairs; Theorem O.12 proves G' <= 1 over Z for cofactors within a factor 4.7913, in particular within one dyadic band, on every dyadic modulus window. CORRECTED PREMISE: this claim previously read '[FM]'s (II) is bilinear over m ~ M and n ~ N, so only banded pairs occur in it'. That paraphrase is NOT what the paper says. (II) sums over (x/2)^theta < m <= x^{theta+nu}, a range of multiplicative width x^nu, which is a band only when nu = 0. The conclusion survives by a better route, verified at source in fm-configuration-is-doubly-banded-at-source: (a) (II) is stated 'for any complex numbers xi_m, kappa_n with |xi_m| <= tau^B(m)', so xi_m = 0 off [M,2M) and kappa_n = 0 off [N,2N) are admissible and (II) therefore IMPLIES every doubly-banded restriction of itself; and (b) the footnote-2 quantity is doubly banded outright, its pair by the footnote's own 'm1, m2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}' and its shared variable by FM's own 'J subset (x/2, x]', since n m1 in J forces x/(2 m1) < n <= x/m1, a ratio of exactly 2. Hence the numerical input to nu = 0 is available over Z directly and does not have to be carried across from Z[i]. The repo's headline -- the obstruction is a theorem about the sequence and survives any change of sieve -- extends to: it survives the change of ring as well, on the configuration that matters.
claims.notes: THE NAMED INFERRED PART IS NOW DISCHARGED, and correcting it also corrected the premise. This claim's notes used to say the inferred part was 'that [FM]'s (II) sees only banded cofactor pairs -- a reading of their quantifier'. Going to the paper settled it, and found the reading was wrong in its literal form: (II)'s m-range is not a band when nu > 0. What makes the conclusion hold is the ARBITRARINESS OF THE COEFFICIENTS, not the shape of the range -- a different mechanism reaching the same place, which is exactly the drift this repo records for paraphrases of sources. The status stays `inferred` only because this claim still depends_on gaussian-to-rational-bridge, which is inferred for a different sentence (the Z[i]-to-Z transfer it is named for). INFERRED, and the inferred part is narrow and named: that [FM]'s (II) sees only banded cofactor pairs. That is a reading of their quantifier, the same reading `gaussian-to-rational-bridge` rests on, and it is not proved here. Everything else is proved -- Note F by the two-line argument over Z[i], O.12 by the Pell/window argument over Z. SCOPE, since 'the Gaussian formulation is not needed' would be too strong: it is not needed FOR THIS STEP. Z[i] remains the repo's working setting for the Type I analysis, the factorisation machinery, and the sieve setup, and O.12's own proof runs on x^2+1's Pell structure rather than on anything ring-free. What changes is that the C4-free input to the Type II conclusion no longer arrives through a bridge; it is available on both sides. NEITHER PROOF IMPLIES THE OTHER, and the id could be read as claiming they do. O.12 gives the 0/1 property over Z on the doubly-dyadic configuration by a Pell/window argument; Note F gives it over Z[i] for all cofactor pairs by the two-line multiplicative argument. The Z statement is NOT a corollary of the Z[i] one -- deducing it is exactly what `gaussian-to-rational-bridge` was for -- and the Z[i] statement is not a special case of the Z one, since O.12 is restricted to banded cofactors and Note F is not. What O.12 removes is the NEED for the transfer on the configuration that matters, not the transfer's content. 'Now proved over Z' must not be read as 'the bridge is closed': the bridge's inference about what (II) ranges over is exactly as it was, and is the whole of this claim's `inferred` status. Raised by the parallel session as the kind of distinction that gets merged later. RENAMED from `the-c4-free-obstruction-does-not-depend-on-the-ring`, which asserted in its id the thing its own notes deny -- that one formulation gives the other. 'Available in both' is what is true. An id is the shortest paraphrase in the repo and the one most often read without the claim attached, so it is where drift costs most.

claims.statement: On Ford-Maynard's footnote-2 configuration -- (II) bands n as well as m -- Theorem O.12 makes #{n : n m_1, n m_2 in J} a 0/1 INDICATOR over Z, not merely bounded. The footnote (arXiv:2407.14368v1 p.7) asks for that count with 'an error term better than O(1)' on average over m_1, m_2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}; for a 0/1 integer that means knowing it exactly. Note F's reading -- the count is 0 or 1, so the error term IS O(1) and no averaging can improve it -- is therefore now available over Z and not only over Z[i]. Measured at X = 12000, mean G over N = 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 falls from the moduli-unrestricted 2.0000, 1.3333, 0.8095, 0.5769, 0.3152 to 1.0000, 0.6667, 0.4762, 0.4103, 0.2319 with max 1 throughout.
claims.notes: THE 'MEAN >= 1' LINE IS THIS REPO'S PARAPHRASE, NOT THE FOOTNOTE'S. Checked at source by the parallel session: the footnote is a condition on the ERROR TERM, and says nothing about a mean exceeding one. So the means below are evidence about how often the count is 1, NOT about a threshold being crossed, and this claim must not be read as defeating the barrier. The real requirement makes the result stronger: pointwise 0/1 is immune to the objection that would sink a mean argument (that a band may hold only two cofactors). REFINES fm-barrier-range-is-small-moduli rather than refuting it: that claim's numbers are correct for the moduli-unrestricted graph and are reproduced here to four places. What changes is which configuration they describe. Its conclusion 'the mean is >= 1 for eps <~ 0.18' holds for the free-modulus reading and NOT for the doubly-banded one, where the cap is structural. And the one value still reaching 1 is a mean over a single pair, which is exactly the informative-subset caution that claim already carries -- now binding on the value that mattered. The max <= 1 half is proved (O.12), not measured; the means are the finite part.

claims.statement: POSITIVE CONTROL for theorem-O12-doubly-dyadic-c4-free. Max Gram on the doubly-dyadic configuration, at Q = 2.5e4 / 5e4 / 1e5: x^2+1 = 1, 1, 1 with 0 banded pairs sharing two throughout (proved, O.12); a^2+b^6 = 6, 7, 11; x^3+2y^3 = 5, 9, 15; a^2+b^4 = 26, 60, 66; a^2+(b^2+1)^2 = 33, 67, 67. So x^2+1 reads exactly 1 at every size while every other sequence reads >= 5 and GROWS with Q. The 0/1 property is not generic.
claims.notes: NOT A CLASSIFIER, AND THE ORDERING IS NOT EVEN STABLE: a^2+b^6 (not known captured) reads 6, 7, 11 against the CAPTURED x^3+2y^3 at 5, 9, 15 -- above at Q = 2.5e4 and below at 5e4 and 1e5. A statistic whose ordering moves with Q cannot separate captured from open, and reading the table as 'low implies hard' would be mean-G-does-not-classify again. x^3+2y^3 is in the table because it is what killed that classifier, and it was run before anything was written. WHAT IS CLAIMED is a difference in KIND, not a position in an ordering: x^2+1 is at 1 with the value a theorem, everything else grows. It also explains the footnote's hedge that bilinear cancellation is difficult 'outside of special situations': for a count ranging over 0..67 there is something to average, for a 0/1 indicator there is not.

claims.statement: For x^2 + c^2 the identity generalises to V W = c^2 M (m_i - m_j) -- derived from a m = X^2 + c^2 and b m = Y^2 + c^2, verified 0 failures over 803, 1112, 1563 pairs at c = 1,2,3 -- and Y > X sqrt(b/a) still holds, so the same route gives |V| < c^2 (M/2 sqrt D)(R - 1/R), a factor c^2 WEAKER. Hence Theorem O.12's threshold scales as 1/c^2: at X_1 = 1 it is M/sqrt(D) > 1.7321/c^2, which falls below what a dyadic band supplies as soon as c >= 2, so THE PROOF DOES NOT EXTEND. The conclusion appears to hold anyway -- banded cofactors share at most one in-window modulus at c = 2 and c = 3, over 530,973 and 617,940 banded pairs at X = 3000. And the two obvious repairs both fail: the bound is SATURATED (max |V| over the bound is 1.0000, 3.9997, 8.9993 at c = 1,2,3, i.e. exactly c^2, so it cannot be tightened), and min |V| is 2, 4, 6, 4, 6 at c = 1..5 -- not c^2, so no |V| >= c^2 lower bound restores the threshold.
claims.notes: A NEGATIVE result, recorded because it saves the attempt and because of how it was produced: derived first, then measured, which is the order the repo's own rule about sweeps and derivations argues for -- and the derivation predicted something FALSE. It said O.12 should fail for c >= 2; measurement says the conclusion holds at c = 2 and 3. So what the derivation actually established is narrower and more useful than the prediction it made: O.12's ARGUMENT is special to c = 1, and the fact is not known to be. That distinction is invisible to measurement alone -- a sweep showing max Gram 1 for all c would have read as 'O.12 generalises', which is exactly what is not established. It also sharpens the parallel session's genericity control from the other side: their table shows the 0/1 property failing badly OFF the line family (>= 11 for a^2+b^4 and the rest), and this shows the PROOF failing within it while the property survives. AND THE MECHANISM FOR c >= 2 CANNOT BE FOUND BY SWEEPING. Having established that the proof fails there while the property holds, the natural next question is what actually forbids the configuration for c >= 2 -- and the natural next measurement is the min |V| over banded in-window pairs sharing two moduli. That set is EMPTY, for every c including c = 1, because it is precisely the configuration the property forbids. I ran it before noticing, ten minutes after agreeing with the parallel session that a conclusion which is a non-occurring configuration cannot be swept for and only its hypotheses can. The earlier min |V| figures -- 2, 4, 6, 4, 6 -- are over all consecutive pairs, which is a different and answerable question, and they are the reason the c^2 repair is known to fail. So: the proof is known not to extend, the property is observed to hold, and why it holds for c >= 2 is open and is not empirically approachable. THIRD DOOR CLOSED, and it nearly opened by reading the wrong statistic. The crude step Y > X sqrt(b/a) is lossy: exactly, (Y/X)^2/(b/a) - 1 = eps = c^2 M/(a b m), a correction that GROWS with c^2 and might have cancelled the c^2 loss. Measured max eps = 1.0000, 4.0000, 8.9999, 15.9997 at c = 1..4 -- i.e. exactly c^2 -- so c^2/(1+eps) = c^2/(1+c^2) < 1 and the threshold would have been restored for every c. But the bound needs the WORST case, which is min eps, and min eps is 2.8e-9, 1.1e-8, 2.7e-8, 4.4e-8: it vanishes as m grows, since eps is inversely proportional to m. So c^2/(1+min eps) = c^2 to four places and nothing is recovered. I computed max first and had the restoration written down. Same informative-subset error as the empty-set sweep above, in the same hour, on the same claim -- max where min was needed.

claims.statement: REFUTED AS EVIDENCE FOR THE TRANSFER. This claim read c = 2..5 as four instances supporting the Gaussian-to-rational transfer. Extending the axis by one shows doubly-dyadic C_4-freeness over Z FAILS at c = 6, with witness cofactors (5,8) -- ratio 1.6 -- and moduli 9, 17 -- ratio 1.889 -- since 5*9 = 3^2+6^2, 8*9 = 6^2+6^2, 5*17 = 7^2+6^2, 8*17 = 10^2+6^2. claims.notes: TWO ERRORS, AND THE SECOND IS MINE ALONE. (1) I stopped the sweep at c = 5 and the parallel session's ran 1,2,3,5,7; neither of us ran 6. Before this the transfer had been tested only on c = 1, which is the case it was built from. So |V| >= 2 extends O.12 to c = 2 and NO FURTHER. Every |V| observed is even at every c from 1 to 5, so |V| >= 2 looks structural, but V-is-even-whenever-M-is-odd is proved for c = 1 only. Honest boundary: c = 1 outright, c = 2 modulo that parity lemma, c >= 3 measured only.

It would have to come from the literature or from a direct argument -- NOT from measuring this sequence more carefully, which is why gaussian-to-rational-bridge and fm-barrier-is-unconditional-at-density-half cannot be promoted by any further work of the kind this repo has been doing. claims.statement: The transfer from C4-freeness over Z[i] to C4-freeness over Z on the doubly-dyadic configuration is NOT automatic, and c = 6 refutes it. A_c = {a+ci} is C4-free over Z[i] for every c. Over Z, banded, the property holds only for c in {1,2,3,4,5,7} and fails at c = 6, 8, 9, ..., 20 -- fourteen of the first twenty -- stable from X = 1500 to 3000 on the survivors. Witness at c = 6: cofactors (5,8) with u = 1.6 < 2 share moduli 9 and 17 with ratio 1.889 < 2, and 5*9 = 45 = 3^2+6^2, 8*9 = 72 = 6^2+6^2, 5*17 = 85 = 7^2+6^2, 8*17 = 136 = 10^2+6^2. The mechanism is the Z[i]/Z gap exactly: (3+6i)(10+6i) = -6+78i and (6+6i)(7+6i) = 6+78i are CONJUGATE, not associate, so there is no Gaussian 4-cycle while the norms coincide at 6120 and the rational cycle is real.
claims.notes: This is the first CONCRETE counterexample the repo has to the transfer pattern, and it changes how the c-family evidence reads. The parallel session's `line-family-tests-the-gaussian-to-rational-transfer` cites c = 2,3,4,5 as four instances where the Z[i] side is proved and the Z side holds; those instances are real, and c = 6 is a refuting instance found by extending the same sweep by one. So the line family does not SUPPORT the transfer -- it BOUNDS it, and the honest evidential base is four supporting against fourteen refuting over c <= 20. Theorem O.12 at c = 1 is therefore not an instance of a general principle about lines; it is specific, which is what my derivation already said about its argument and now holds of the fact. It does NOT refute `gaussian-to-rational-bridge` for x^2+1: there the Z-side statement is PROVED by O.12 rather than transferred, so the bridge's numerical content does not rely on the pattern that fails here. What it removes is any reading of the c-family as evidence that the pattern is reliable.

claims.statement: For f(x) = x^2 + D, four consecutive arguments give a 4-cycle exactly when D = k^2 + 3k + 1. Identity: (k^2+D)((k+3)^2+D) - ((k+1)^2+D)((k+2)^2+D) = 4(D - k^2 - 3k - 1), verified 0 failures over 40 x 199 (k,D) pairs. So the family D = 1, 5, 11, 19, 29, 41, 55, ... all carry the cycle, and exactly two members escape being DOUBLY DYADIC counterexamples: k = 0, D = 1, whose values are 1, 2, 5, 10 -- the first is the UNIT modulus, which no Type II hypothesis admits -- and k = 1, D = 5, whose modulus ratio 14/6 = 2.333 exceeds 2. For every k >= 2 both ratios are below 2 and falling toward 1: (cofactor, modulus) = (1.333, 1.800) at D = 11, (1.250, 1.571) at 19, (1.200, 1.444) at 29. x^2+1 IS the k = 0 member.
claims.notes: The sharpest form the repo has of WHY x^2+1 is special, and it is not a coincidence of small numbers. Doubly-dyadic C4-freeness -- Theorem O.12's conclusion -- fails for an infinite explicit family of degree-2 sequences, and x^2+1 escapes for exactly the reason the unit cofactor is excluded everywhere else in this repo: its member of the family has 0^2+1 = 1 as one of the four values. D = 5 escapes for a second and unrelated reason, the modulus ratio, which is why the first genuine counterexample is D = 11 rather than D = 5. Found by extending an axis nobody had extended -- D itself -- after the same move on c found the c = 6 failure. Note that a sweep over D would have shown the failures without the identity; what the identity adds is that the family is infinite, explicit, and that x^2+1's membership in it is degenerate rather than absent. THE PICTURE COMPLETES, and the consecutive family is the right one to have isolated. In general (a^2+D)(d^2+D) = (b^2+D)(c^2+D) holds iff D = (b^2 c^2 - a^2 d^2)/(a^2 + d^2 - b^2 - c^2), and every one of the 16 D <= 40 that fail doubly-dyadic C4-freeness is realised by an explicit quadruple -- 16 of 16, found by direct search. But a cycle is not automatically DOUBLY DYADIC: the sub-family a,b,c,d = 1,2,n,n+1 gives D = (3n+1)/2 for odd n, so D = 17 at n = 11 carries the cycle 18*161 = 21*138 = 2898, and its cofactor ratio is 21/18 = 1.167 while its MODULUS ratio is 138/18 = 7.67. D = 17 duly appears in the holds list. So the general form explains which D carry a cycle at all, and CONSECUTIVE arguments are what make the four values close enough for both ratios to fall below 2. That is why the k^2+3k+1 family is the one that matters and why x^2+1 sitting at its k = 0 is the whole of its escape.

claims.statement: Conjecture O.2's analogue and Theorem O.12's analogue are BOTH false for x^2+39, in one configuration. Cofactors (5,8) -- ratio 1.6, inside one dyadic band -- share the three moduli 8, 11, 15, all inside one dyadic window since 15 < 16: 5*8 = 40 = 1^2+39, 5*11 = 55 = 4^2+39, 5*15 = 75 = 6^2+39, 8*8 = 64 = 5^2+39, 8*11 = 88 = 7^2+39, 8*15 = 120 = 9^2+39. All six verified. Over D <= 60 there are seven unit-free triples in a window -- D = 29, 39, 42, 44, 52, 53, 59 -- and D = 1 is not among them. (D = 29 is cofactors (3,1235), moduli 10, 15, 18, also verified term by term.) Excluding the unit cofactor matters: 35 of 60 admit a triple if the unit is allowed, and the unit is what no Type II hypothesis admits.
claims.notes: DOES NOT REFUTE O.2 OR O.12 FOR x^2+1. Both stand exactly as they were: O.12 proved, O.2 open with no counterexample to X = 8000 and a two-step floor unmoved at 13.0000 from X = 1500 to 8000. What it removes is any reading of them as instances of something general. The twelve theorems of the Note O thread establish a fact about x^2+1, not about degree-2 sequences -- and now that is demonstrated rather than assumed, by an explicit banded triple at D = 39 with cofactors as small as 5 and 8. Same correction the D = k^2+3k+1 family makes for the 4-cycle, one level up: there x^2+1 was the degenerate member of a failing family, here it is simply not in the failing set at all. Found by extending the D axis to the triple question after it had paid off twice on the pair question.

claims.statement: Doubly-dyadic C_4-freeness for a quadratic depends only on its DISCRIMINANT. Completing the square, 4(x^2+bx+c) = (2x+b)^2 + |Delta| with Delta = b^2-4c, so a general quadratic is x^2 + D on arguments of one parity, up to a factor 4. Checked at X = 900 over 0 <= b <= 3, 1 <= c <= 7: every discriminant class agrees internally -- Delta = -3, -4, -7, -8, -12, -15 all read banded max 1 (two polynomials each), and Delta = -11 and -19 both read 2 (two polynomials each). So the line family x^2+c^2 (Delta = -4c^2), the D family x^2+D (Delta = -4D) and the general quadratics are ONE axis indexed by Delta, with x^2+1 at Delta = -4.
claims.notes: A SMALL-COFACTOR SEARCH IS NOT AN EFFECTIVE DETECTOR, and I concluded it was. Searching cofactors <= 300 with values <= 3e6 finds D = 11 at (3,4) with moduli 5, 9; D = 14 at (3,5); D = 19 at (4,5); D = 39 at (5,8) -- every witness below cofactor 9 -- while D = 2..10, 12, 13, 15..18, 20 show nothing. From that I concluded failures announce themselves at tiny cofactors and the survivors' persistence was therefore meaningful. WRONG: D = 35's witness has cofactors (2249, 3756), three orders of magnitude above my bound, and D = 35 held at X = 1500 before failing at X = 2500. So the tiny-cofactor pattern is a property of the D I happened to find, not of failure, and my bounded search could not have seen the case that refutes it. Same error as the axis lesson, one level in: I bounded a search and read the bound's silence as evidence. D = 1 remains the only value PROVED to hold. THE FAILURES ANNOUNCE THEMSELVES AT TINY COFACTORS, which makes the survivors' persistence meaningful rather than a sweep artefact. Searching cofactors <= 300 with values <= 3e6: D = 11 fails at cofactors (3,4) with moduli 5, 9; D = 14 at (3,5) with 6, 10; D = 19 at (4,5) with 7, 11; and D = 39 at (5,8) with 8, 11, 15. Every witness has both cofactors below 9. Meanwhile D = 2..10, 12, 13, 15..18, 20 show NOTHING over that range -- so the earlier caution that the small-D survivors might simply be under-swept is weakened, though not removed: D = 1 remains the only one PROVED to hold, by O.12, and a search bounded at cofactor 300 cannot rule out a witness above it. SO THE CORRECT DIAGNOSIS IS NOT 'size arguments cannot see the arithmetic' BUT 'bounds stated for all configurations are loose by the width of the configurations that do not occur'. Restricted to the realised type the size argument is attained to a third of a percent. The three instances above are all cases where a bound ADMITS something nature declines; this is the one case where the restricted bound is tight, and it is the only one found. THE 0.33% CARRIES A CONDITION AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED BARE. It is sharpness against the |V| >= 2 threshold, and |V| >= 2 binds only because every realised extremum measured is a tau_1 step -- MEASURED ABSENCE OVER A FINITE RANGE, not a theorem. The non-tau_1 case is the cross-orbit configuration multipliers do not predict (at (1,115921) the multiplier product predicts a modulus ratio of 1.31 against an observed minimum of 33.77), so the gap between O.12's 4.7913 and 33.9706 is NAMED, not closed.
