That is worth saying and is a different statement from 'exactly', which would invite a reader to conclude the bound is tight there. So the honest summary of the thread is not 'these theorems nearly close O.2' but 'the size arguments are now sharp enough to be worth stating and are still nowhere near what is true, and the gap between them is arithmetic nobody here has reached'.

claims.statement: Note L's eps and Note O's tau are different group actions on the same solution set of a Y^2 - b X^2 = M, and neither note relates them. eps -- the fundamental automorph, u^2 - D v^2 = 1 -- moves WITHIN an orbit, and Prop L.1's spacing m'/m -> eps^2 >= phi^4 = 6.854 is why a window holds at most one member of each orbit. tau_k -- the multiplier, U^2 = M^2 + 4k^2 D -- moves BETWEEN orbits, and tau_1^2 can sit well below 2, which is how two moduli land in one window. At (1,41), Note L's own windowed witness: eps = 2049 + 320 sqrt41 = 4098 so within-orbit m'/m ~ 1.7e7, while tau_1 = (42 + 2 sqrt41)/40 = 1.37016 and tau_1^2 = 1.87733 against an observed 1370/730 = 1.87671 -- four places, the gap being the finite '+1' correction. So the two moduli in that window are in DIFFERENT orbits, brought together by tau and not by eps.
claims.notes: Makes the whole structure legible and explains why the two notes never collided: the windowed Gram entry counts ORBITS that tau reaches inside one window, with eps guaranteeing at most one member per orbit, and Conjecture O.2 is the statement that tau never reaches three. I nearly got this backwards -- I assigned moduli to orbits by |V| = 2, reasoning that the fundamental multiplier is the fundamental automorph, and measured 'two moduli of one orbit in a window', which would have contradicted Prop L.1. The arithmetic at (1,41) is what separated them: 1.877 against 1.7e7 is not a near miss. Prop L.1's own hedge stands -- its spacing is asymptotic ('x'/x -> eps') and the note already records the proved bound as O_eps(N^eps) with the constant 2 rigorous_finite.

claims.statement: A triple needs a class admitting at least TWO in-window multipliers -- indices k with M^2 + 4k^2 D a perfect square and tau_k^2 < 2 -- and at X = 3000 only 43 of 1,815,155 classes do. The distribution is 1,503,796 admitting none, 311,316 admitting one, 43 admitting two, none admitting three. Of the 43, FORTY have exactly one realised modulus and THREE have exactly two; none has three, so no chain is realised. The three are (1,423125) with k = 1,91 and moduli 10,17; (1,51701) with k = 1,33 and moduli 82,145; (53,423125) with k = 1,12 and moduli 10,17 -- exactly the live non-fundamental close pairs identified independently much earlier by exp14. AND IT SCALES, measured at three sizes: chain-admitting classes are 23 of 453,111 at X = 1500, 43 of 1,815,155 at X = 3000, 78 of 7,267,040 at X = 6000. The count grows 23 -> 43 -> 78 while the class population grows 4x per doubling, so the FRACTION halves each time -- 5.1e-5, 2.4e-5, 1.07e-5. Within the chain-admitting set the modulus counts are {1: 23} at 1500, {1: 40, 2: 3} at 3000, {1: 73, 2: 5} at 6000. None has three moduli at any size.
claims.notes: Makes O.2's content at a given X completely explicit, and the reduction is severe: 1.8 million classes down to 43, then to 3 once the moduli have to exist, then to 0 because none of the 3 has a third modulus. The population that matters is 'classes admitting two in-window multipliers', which is 43 -- not classes with three moduli (60) and not all classes (1.8M). And the three that realise a k >= 2 step are the SAME three exp14 found as the live non-fundamental close pairs, from a completely different construction: exp14 searched the realised side by streaming enumeration, this counts multiplier indices satisfying a Pell condition. Two routes, same three configurations, which is the strongest confirmation either has. No law is fitted to 23 -> 43 -> 78; the values are recorded, per the repo's rule about order-statements read as equalities. What is worth stating without a fit is the DIRECTION: the chain-admitting fraction halves per doubling of X while the absolute count roughly doubles, so the set where a triple is even structurally possible is growing far more slowly than the classes are. And the moduli needed to use a chain never materialise -- the maximum over all three sizes is two, against the three a triple requires. TWO COUNTS, NOT ONE, and X = 3000 could not show the difference. 'Realises two moduli' and 'realises two moduli IN ONE WINDOW' are different, and they first diverge at X = 6000: of the five chain-admitting classes with two moduli, FOUR are in one window -- (1,423125) 10,17; (1,51701) 82,145; (53,423125) 10,17; (37,26245) 545,986 -- while (13,27145) has moduli 2 and 530, a ratio of 265. At X = 3000 all three coincided, so the smaller table conflates them. Raised by the parallel session; verified here. Note also that (37,26245) is a FOURTH live close pair, not among the three exp14 found at X = 3000.

claims.statement: Grouping a class's shared moduli into automorph orbits has no cheap criterion, and the two obvious candidates both fail. (1) The ORDER'S FUNDAMENTAL UNIT is wrong: for (1,5) the form is Y^2 - 5X^2 = 4 and the observed modulus ratios are 5, 6.5, 6.8, 6.8462, 6.8529, 6.8539, 6.8541 converging to phi^4 = 6.8541, so the automorph is phi^2 = 2.6180 -- which lies in Z[phi] and NOT in Z[sqrt5], whose fundamental unit 9+4sqrt5 = 17.9443 would predict a ratio of 322 and split one orbit into many. (2) M | V is wrong in the opposite direction: at (1,5) with m = 2, 10 we have V = -2 and M = 4, so M does not divide V, yet the two are in the SAME orbit. That is forced rather than accidental -- the subcase alternates along an orbit (Prop O.6), and p | V holds exactly when the subcases agree, so consecutive orbit members necessarily have M not dividing V.
claims.notes: Recorded as an obstacle rather than a result, because the parallel session asked for a measurement that needs this grouping -- the minimum ratio spanning three populated orbits, and whether that margin shrinks as the orbit count grows -- and I would rather report that I cannot compute it reliably than produce a number from a wrong grouping. That is the near-miss recorded one claim earlier, arriving again within the hour: a plausible identification between two pieces of machinery, which here would have silently mis-partitioned the moduli and produced a margin that measures nothing. The correct criterion is the automorph of the FORM, which depends on the discriminant and on which order the relevant unit lives in, and is a real computation rather than a one-line test.

claims.statement: A triple needs a class admitting TWO in-window multipliers (indices k with M^2 + 4k^2 D a perfect square and tau_k^2 < 2). At X = 3000, over 1,815,155 reduced ratio classes: 1,503,796 with none, 311,316 with one, 43 with two, ZERO with three or more. Of the 43, forty realise exactly one modulus, three realise two, none three. So O.2's entire content at this X lives on 43 classes, and in 40 of them the moduli do not exist to use the multipliers they admit. The three realising a k >= 2 step are exactly exp14's live non-fundamental close pairs: (1,423125) k = 1,91 moduli 10,17; (1,51701) k = 1,33 moduli 82,145; (53,423125) k = 1,12 moduli 10,17.
claims.notes: TWO OF THE THREE THRESHOLDS ARE ONE FORMULA. |V| >= V0 requires M/sqrtD > 2 sqrt2 V0, so with M/sqrtD = (u-1)/sqrt(u) the threshold is u > (sqrt2 V0 + sqrt(2 V0^2 + 1))^2: V0 = 2 gives 33.970563, V0 = 4 gives 129.992307, V0 = 6 gives 289.996552, V0 = 8 gives 513.998054, running to 8 V0^2 + 2 from below with gaps 0.029, 0.008, 0.003, 0.002. IT CLOSES AT THE SEAM: sqrt2*2 + sqrt9 = 2sqrt2 + 3 = (1+sqrt2)^2 exactly (verified symbolically), so V0 = 2 gives u > (1+sqrt2)^4 on the nose. The doubling 4sqrt2 -> 8sqrt2 is therefore |V| >= 2 -> |V| >= 4, one input read twice rather than two derivations agreeing. BUT THE TRIPLE THRESHOLD IS NOT IN THE FAMILY: 133.874781 falls strictly between V0 = 4 (129.992) and V0 = 5 (201.995), because it comes from O.4's composite tau_1^2 < sqrt2 and not from a |V| bound. Two rows are one mechanism, the third is another, and their interleaving is a consistency check rather than a pattern. THREE THRESHOLDS, ONE CONSTANT, all conditions on M/sqrt(D) = (u-1)/sqrt(u): a PAIR in one window needs M/sqrtD > 4sqrt2 = 5.6569, i.e. u > 33.9706 = (1+sqrt2)^4; a CHAIN (second in-window multiplier, k >= 2) needs 8sqrt2 = 11.3137, i.e. u > 129.9923 = (4sqrt2+sqrt33)^2; a TRIPLE (O.4) needs 4(2^(1/4)+2^(3/4)) = 11.4840, i.e. u > 133.8748. All verified to six places. The chain sits 3.8825 BELOW the triple, exactly as it must since a triple needs a chain and more. AND THAT IS WHY THE SET IS EMPTY: the two requirements pull opposite ways. Max shared-modulus count by u at X = 3000 is 2 / 8 / 6 / 4 / 3 over u < 2 / 2-10 / 10-100 / 100-1e3 / >1e3 (classes 530,837 / 710,187 / 392,697 / 124,151 / 57,283). A chain needs u > 130 and the modulus count FALLS with u, so the range where a chain is possible is where the moduli to use it are scarcest. NOT ESTABLISHED AS STRUCTURAL: three moduli do occur above u = 1e3, so modulus count alone does not forbid a triple; what is established is quantified tension, not decisiveness. Also: (37,26245) at moduli 545, 986 is a FOURTH live close pair, not among exp14's three, and only visible at X = 6000. SCALES, AND THE FRACTION HALVES PER DOUBLING, all three rows reproduced independently: at X = 1500, 3000, 6000 the classes are 453,111 / 1,815,155 / 7,267,040 and the counts with two in-window multipliers are 23 / 43 / 78, i.e. fractions 5.1e-5, 2.4e-5, 1.07e-5. Moduli realised: {1:23}, {1:40, 2:3}, {1:73, 2:5} -- maximum TWO at every size against the three a triple needs. No law is fitted to 23/43/78; the values are the statement and only the direction is claimed. CAUTION: 'realises two moduli' and 'realises two moduli IN ONE WINDOW' are different counts and first diverge at X = 6000, where four of the five are in one window ((1,423125) 10,17; (1,51701) 82,145; (53,423125) 10,17; (37,26245) 545,986) and (13,27145) has moduli 2 and 530, a ratio of 265. At X = 3000 all three coincided, so the smaller table cannot show the distinction. THREE INDEPENDENT CONSTRUCTIONS, SAME THREE CONFIGURATIONS: exp14 streaming the realised side; the parallel session counting multiplier indices against a Pell condition; and a re-derivation here reproducing 1,503,796 / 311,316 / 43 and the same k values exactly. FOURTH REFINEMENT OF O.2's DENOMINATOR, each correct against its predecessor: 278,939 above threshold -> 31 informative -> 60 with three shared moduli -> 43 admitting two in-window multipliers. Each shrank because a necessary condition was noticed, not because the data changed. IT REPLACES an orbit-margin measurement that could not be computed: partitioning moduli into automorph orbits has no cheap criterion and both obvious ones fail in opposite directions -- the order's fundamental unit is wrong (at (1,5) the automorph is phi^2, in the maximal order Z[phi], not Z[sqrt5]'s 9+4sqrt5 = 17.94, which would predict 322 and shatter one orbit into many), and M | V is wrong the other way (at (1,5), m = 2 and 10 lie in the SAME orbit with M nmid V, which the subcase alternation forces for consecutive members). A mis-partition produces a margin that measures nothing and looks exactly like a margin.

claims.statement: A second in-window multiplier requires b/a > (4 sqrt2 + sqrt33)^2 = 129.9923. tau_k^2 < 2 needs k < 0.17678 M/sqrt(D) asymptotically, so k >= 2 needs M/sqrt(D) > 8 sqrt2 = 11.3137 -- the same constant as O.12's asymptotic bound and the corrected Plucker value, being |V| >= 4 read as k >= 2. With M/sqrt(D) = (u-1)/sqrt(u), solving v^2 - 8 sqrt2 v - 1 = 0 at v = sqrt(u) gives v = 4 sqrt2 + sqrt33 = 11.401417 and u > 129.9923, against O.4's asymptotic triple threshold of 133.8748. The chain threshold sits 3.88 below, as it must: a triple needs a chain and more. AND THE WHOLE TABLE IS ONE FORMULA. |V| >= V0 requires M/sqrt(D) > 2 sqrt2 V0, so u > (sqrt2 V0 + sqrt(2 V0^2 + 1))^2: at V0 = 2 that is (1+sqrt2)^4 = 33.9706, the PAIR threshold, since sqrt2*2 + sqrt9 = 2sqrt2+3 = (1+sqrt2)^2 exactly; at V0 = 4 it is (4sqrt2+sqrt33)^2 = 129.9923, the CHAIN threshold; and it continues 289.9966 at V0 = 6 and 513.9981 at V0 = 8. So the doubling 4sqrt2 -> 8sqrt2 between pair and chain is exactly |V| >= 2 -> |V| >= 4. Expanding, u = 4V0^2 + 1 + 2 sqrt2 V0 sqrt(2V0^2+1), which approaches 8 V0^2 + 2 FROM BELOW with the gap falling 0.029, 0.008, 0.003, 0.002.
claims.notes: Gives the mechanism behind the emptiness, because the two requirements for a triple pull in opposite directions. A chain needs u > 130; but the maximum modulus count over all classes FALLS with u -- 8 at u in [2,10), 6 at [10,100), 4 at [100,1000), 3 above 1000 at X = 3000 -- so the range where a chain is possible is exactly the range where the moduli to use it are scarcest. The 43 chain-admitting classes have at most two, against the three a triple needs. Whether that opposition is structural or an accident of this range is NOT established: 3 moduli do occur above u = 1000, so modulus count alone does not forbid a triple. The unification came from the parallel session tabulating three thresholds side by side -- pair (1+sqrt2)^4, chain (4sqrt2+sqrt33)^2, triple 133.8748 -- at which point the 4sqrt2 / 8sqrt2 doubling was visible and turned out to be the |V| input rather than a coincidence of two derivations. The triple threshold is NOT in the family: it comes from O.4's composite tau_1^2 < sqrt2 rather than from a |V| bound, which is why it sits 3.88 above the chain instead of at a lattice point of the formula.

claims.statement: The strongest form of 'kappa cannot see the obstruction'. For x^2 + D the sequence has |A| = X and Q = X^2 + D, so kappa = X^2/(X^2+D) -> 1 for EVERY fixed D. At X = 10^4 the whole family sits within 4e-7 of 1 -- kappa = 0.999999990 at D = 1 against 0.999999610 at D = 39, a spread in the NINTH decimal. Meanwhile D decides the structure completely: D = 1, 2 hold unconditionally, D = 4 holds on parity, and D = 6, 11, 19, 36, 39 fail with explicit witnesses, D = 39 with a banded triple. So an entire one-parameter family has kappa -> 1 throughout and splits into proved-holds and proved-fails. AND kappa IS NOT EVEN MONOTONE IN THE PROPERTY. For k x^2 + D, kappa = X^2/(k X^2 + D) -> 1/k, so the LEADING coefficient does move it. Measured at X = 1200: kappa = 1 holds for x^2+1 and FAILS for x^2+39 -- same kappa, opposite outcomes -- while kappa = 1/2 holds for both 2x^2+1 and 2x^2+39, and kappa = 1/3 holds for 3x^2+39. So the sequence with the SMALLER kappa holds exactly where the larger one fails. No monotone relation in either direction: kappa neither predicts the property nor anti-predicts it.
claims.notes: Stronger than the two earlier demonstrations, and in the way that matters. 'kappa counts lines' explains why the A_B threshold coincidence carries no information; 'two points flip C4-freeness at fixed kappa' needs an O(1) PERTURBATION of the sequence, which a reader can dismiss as artificial. This needs no perturbation at all -- x^2+D are natural sequences, one per D, and the parameter kappa cannot resolve is the parameter that decides the answer. Found by placing two finished results next to each other, the D axis and the kappa formula, both already recorded and neither computed for this purpose. The one arithmetic slip is worth noting: I first asserted kappa > 0.99999 across the family, which fails at X = 10^3 where kappa(39) = 0.999961. Caught by the test, not by reading. The k-direction has a known mechanism and it points the WRONG way, which is why the non-monotonicity is not a surprise once seen: k imposes k | M D, thinning the class population and TIGHTENING the structure, while kappa = 1/k FALLS with k. So larger k means smaller kappa and a tighter sequence -- density and structure moving in opposite directions along the one axis kappa can see. Through D, kappa is blind; through k, it is inverted. That is the whole of what kappa can resolve about a degree-2 sequence, and neither component carries the property.

claims.statement: The D axis matters only at degree 2. Measured at X = 900: x^3 + D is doubly-dyadic C4-free for D = 1, 2, 6, 11, 19, 29, 39 -- every value tested -- while x^2 + D fails at D = 11 with cofactors (3,4) and moduli 5,9; at D = 19 with (4,5) and 7,11; and at D = 39 with (8,11) and 5,8. So the D-dependence that governs degree 2 is absent one degree up. The invariant a Y^d - b X^d = M*D holds at every degree, but the Pell/multiplier machinery that converts it into a threshold does not, and at d = 3 the graph is too thin for coincidences regardless of D -- Note L's ladder gives kappa = X^{2-d}, so kappa -> 0 at d = 3 against kappa -> 1/k at d = 2.
claims.notes: Completes the connection between the degree ladder and the D axis: DEGREE controls density, D controls structure WITHIN degree 2, and at degree >= 3 the density is already too low for D to have anything to act on. Which is another way of saying degree 2 is the only place any of this is a question -- consistent with the ladder's own finding that d = 1 is solved and d >= 3 is thinner than the sieve needs. Measured at one size only, X = 900, where x^3+D values already reach 7e8; the sparsity argument makes larger X unlikely to change it, but that is reasoning and not measurement. Also worth noting the D = 39 witness here, cofactors (8,11) with moduli 5,8, is the SAME four values as the (5,8) with moduli 8,11 found earlier -- cofactors and moduli exchanged, so the configuration is symmetric.

claims.statement: BOTH analytic quantities this repo measures are blind to the D axis. kappa = X^2/(kX^2+D) -> 1/k cannot resolve D at all. And the Mobius side is no better: |sum_{x<=X} mu(x^2+D)|/sqrt(X) at X = 20000 and 40000 is 0.4950/0.2100 at D = 1 (HOLDS), 0.2546/0.4450 at D = 2 (HOLDS), 1.3506/0.9200 at D = 6 (holds, asymptotically protected), 0.2687/0.0250 at D = 11 (FAILS), and 1.5698/1.0800 at D = 39 (FAILS, with a banded triple). Every value is O(1) -- square-root cancellation uniformly in D -- and the ordering matches the structure at neither size: the two largest are D = 6, which holds, and D = 39, which fails worst.
claims.notes: The sharpest form of this repo's own position, reached by placing the mu side next to the D axis -- the third deliberate adjacency and the third to pay. Note F says the obstruction is ARITHMETIC rather than density; Note J says the difficulty is in the absolute values. This says the arithmetic parameter that decides the whole C4 structure is invisible to BOTH analytic measures available here. No law is fitted and none should be: the point is the ABSENCE of a relation, and O(1) fluctuation is exactly what square-root cancellation predicts for every D alike. Five values of D at two sizes. REFINED, and the refinement is a caution rather than a correction. The parallel session measured the mu-weighted OFF and found it blind -- signs reshuffling between bands -- but reported that mean G and DIAG DO see D, concluding the dichotomy is weighted/unweighted rather than analytic/structural. On the repo's canonical incidence (polyseq.incidence with coeffs = (D,0,1), min_cofactor=1, X = 4000) I get something different: the OFF-DIAGONAL mean is 0.0136, 0.0121, 0.0099, 0.0110, 0.0126 at D = 1,2,6,11,39 with 9-27% drift between bands [1000,2000) and [2500,5000), and max G = 2 for every D -- a D-range comparable to the band drift, i.e. NO clean separation. What does grow with D is the DIAGONAL: moduli per cofactor 1.4709, 1.5246, 1.5142, 1.6522, 1.6993. So the 'matrix sees D' reading is carried by the diagonal, and the off-diagonal -- which is what C4-freeness and the Type II cancellation are about -- does not clearly see it. I could not reproduce their 1.008-1.21 figures on this construction and do not know which differs; recorded as a discrepancy rather than a correction of either.

claims.statement: Note M's theta = 1/2 and Note L's Gram-mean minimum are the same place. Note M measures the mu-saving as Q^{(1/2-theta)/2}, exactly zero at theta = 1/2, so the cancellation available to a Type II estimate vanishes there. Note L measures mean G over cofactor bands as U-shaped with its minimum at N = 1.37 X, from an independent divisor-built incidence table. Converting: with m n = Q ~ X^2 a cofactor N = 1.37 X is a modulus m = Q/N, giving theta = 0.48034, 0.48191, 0.48633, 0.48861 at X = 3000, 6000, 1e5, 1e6 -- rising to 1/2. So the scale where no cancellation is available is the scale where there are fewest edges to cancel over.
claims.notes: Fourth deliberate adjacency, and across halves like the other three that paid -- an analytic measurement against a combinatorial one. The mechanism is not mysterious and should be stated: both are governed by the balanced split m = n = sqrt(Q), where the saving exponent vanishes BY CONSTRUCTION and the Gram U-shape bottoms for structural reasons. What is worth recording is that the two were measured by completely different routes -- one from mu sums over progressions, one from a divisor-built incidence table -- and neither note observes that they land together. The convergence to 1/2 is from BELOW and is still 0.4886 at X = 1e6, so the coincidence is asymptotic rather than exact at any measured size.

claims.statement: The D-blindness is a property of the mu WEIGHTS, not of the analytic side. OFF = sum_{x != y} mu(x^2+D) mu(y^2+D) G_M(x,y) is an ELEMENT-indexed incidence matrix, mu-weighted -- G_M(x,y) = #{m ~ M : m | x^2+D and m | y^2+D}, NOT Note F / Prop L.1's cofactor-indexed #{m : m n1, m n2 in A}; the two are different matrices and CLAUDE.md conflated them. so weighted and unweighted readings of the SAME incidence matrix are exactly comparable in one pass. At X = 20000 over bands [1000,2000) and [2500,5000), OFF/DIAG is +0.2275/+0.1441 (D=1), +0.0906/-0.0468 (D=2), -0.1099/-0.0912 (D=6), -0.1604/+0.0714 (D=11), +0.1892/+0.1257 (D=39): it changes sign WITHIN each band and its sign PATTERN is unstable BETWEEN them (+,+,-,-,+ against +,-,-,+,+), so it cannot be monotone in D. But the same matrix unweighted is not blind: mean G is 1.0077, 1.0482, 1.0655, 1.2127, 1.1919 in band 1 and reproduces to under 1% in band 2, and DIAG swings 4x (5073, 5188, 7644, 1908, 2030). So the dichotomy is WEIGHTED vs UNWEIGHTED, not analytic vs structural -- DIAG is on the analytic side and sees D fine. The D-dependence is present in the object the analytic quantity is built from, and the mu signs annihilate it.
claims.notes: Note J from a new angle: the signs that make the sum hard to bound are the same signs that hide the arithmetic; one mechanism with a measurement on both faces. The parallel session's S_mu column was reproduced here to all five digits from an independent sieve before this was built on it. TWO CAUTIONS, both about the unweighted statistic. (i) From band 1 alone max G is monotone in D (4,7,9,10,15) and was written up as 'climbs monotonically'; band 2 gives 4,8,7,9,14, which is neither monotone nor band-stable. Quote the mean, not the max. (ii) mean G is NOT a structural classifier and must not be read as a severity ordering: its order is 1 < 2 < 6 < 39 < 11, putting D = 11 ABOVE D = 39 while 39 is structurally the more degenerate (a banded TRIPLE against 11's banded 4-cycle). This repo already refuted mean G as a captured/uncaptured classifier from two points confirmed on two more; the same statistic is now available for the same misreading on a new axis, and the temptation is stronger because it reproduces across bands to under 1%. Reproducibility is not aboutness. SCOPE, added after the parallel session could not reproduce the mean and we found we were measuring different matrices: this is a statement about the Cauchy-Schwarz chain, NOT about C4-freeness. On the same values in one window [1000,2000) at X = 3000, the COFACTOR Gram (the C4 object) has max exactly 2 for every D in {1,2,6,11,39} and mean over supported pairs 1.0245, 1.0222, 1.0220, 1.0188, 1.0149 -- flat, in fact slightly falling -- while the ELEMENT matrix has max 2,4,5,7,6 and mean 1.0043, 1.0427, 1.0521, 1.1944, 1.1656. So the structural matrix is blind to D and the one inside OFF is not. Our two readings ALSO used different denominators (mean over supported pairs ~1.02 against mean over all pairs ~0.015), so the disagreement was disguised twice over.

claims.statement: The D-dependence is not an artefact of the corner a Type II hypothesis excludes. Every witness found first had one variable tiny -- D = 11 at cofactors (3,4), D = 39 at (5,8) -- so the natural worry is that the whole axis lives where the hypothesis does not look. Requiring cofactors >= 200 AND moduli >= 200 at X = 4000, four of D <= 40 still fail: D = 23 at cofactors (1131,1432) ratio 1.266 with moduli (6672,9617) ratio 1.441; D = 31 at (1055,1808) 1.714 with (625,1120) 1.792; D = 35 at (2249,3756) 1.670 with (459,879) 1.915; D = 39 at (781,1180) 1.511 with (688,880) 1.279. All banded on both axes, all sixteen products verified, and D = 1 is not among them. The D = 39 case: 781*688 = 733^2+39, 781*880 = 829^2+39, 1180*688 = 901^2+39, 1180*880 = 1019^2+39.
claims.notes: Answers the objection that would have sunk the whole D axis, and I nearly concluded the opposite. Having found that the singly-windowed cofactor Gram is flat in D and that the canonical incidence with its default cofactor floor gives max G = 1 for every D, the natural reading was 'the D-dependence lives in small cofactors, which Type II excludes'. Checking it showed 13 of 40 D have failures with both COFACTORS large -- but those have tiny MODULI, so they are not Type II shapes either. Only requiring BOTH scales large settles it, and four survive. Sharpens the parallel session's observation that the structure's D-sensitivity needs both variables banded: it needs them banded AND large, and it survives both.

claims.statement: O.12's proved threshold (5+sqrt21)/2 = 4.7913 is not approached. The smallest cofactor ratio realising a windowed 4-cycle for x^2+1 is 34.0811, at cofactors (37, 1261) sharing moduli 866 and 1730 -- 37*866 = 179^2+1, 37*1730 = 253^2+1, 1261*866 = 1045^2+1, 1261*1730 = 1477^2+1, moduli ratio 1.99769 so one window -- and this minimum is UNCHANGED across X = 1500, 3000, 6000, 12000, a factor of 8 with no smaller witness appearing. So O.12 is loose by 7.11x with no sign of the bound being approached. This also improves the witness the notes quote: (2, 82) at ratio 41 is not extremal. Both are unit-free.
claims.notes: The size-argument theme of the O-thread made quantitative on the one theorem that touches the main line. CLAUDE.md already said 'the size arguments are sharp enough to state and still nowhere near what is true'; this is that gap as a number, 7.11x, for O.12 specifically. Found by asking for the MINIMUM where the notes had recorded an EXAMPLE -- the integer max Gram says only whether the bound is violated, while the extremal ratio says how much room is left, and nobody had asked. The stability is the finding rather than the value: a minimum that does not move across a factor of 8 in X is evidence the extremal configuration is not drifting toward the bound. CAVEAT, per this repo's own rule: this is a minimum over a finite range and a bound's silence is not evidence about what lies outside it. X = 12000 reaches values 1.44e8; a smaller-ratio witness beyond that is not excluded. THE UNIT COFACTOR IS THE MINIMISER FOR SOME D and the experiment reports both columns because of it: at D = 2 the overall minimum is 33.0000 at (1, 33) with moduli 6, 11 -- inadmissible for any Type II hypothesis -- while the unit-free minimum is 34.0548 at (73, 2486) with moduli 1707, 3411, slack 7.11x. At D = 1 the minimum is already unit-free. Recording the two unit-free values, 34.0811 and 34.0548, as VALUES: they give the same slack to three figures, and with two points no law is fitted and none should be. The margin is also worth stating the other way round: a banded pair needs ratio < 2, O.12 proves > 4.7913 (a factor 2.40 of margin), and nature supplies 34.08 (a factor 17.04). The theorem buys 2.4x where 17x is true. CORRECTS A RECORDED NUMBER: Note O previously gave the observed minimum as 43.79 at (34,1489) with moduli 1073 and 1973. That pair is genuine but not minimal; 34.0811 at (37,1261) is. The cause is the anchored-window defect -- 866 and 1730 have ratio 1.9977 and lie in one dyadic window, but a sweep stepping M = 2,4,8,... puts them in [512,1024) and [1024,2048) and never compares them, while 1073 and 1973 both sit in [1024,2048). Third recorded instance of that defect, and the first to corrupt a value rather than a coverage figure.

claims.statement: Proposition O.13. A 4-cycle whose two shared moduli are related by the fundamental multiplier tau_1 lies in one dyadic window only if the cofactor ratio satisfies u = b/a > (1+sqrt2)^4 = 17 + 12*sqrt2 = 33.970563... . Proof: the modulus ratio is tau_1^2 and a window needs tau_1^2 < 2, i.e. (sqrt u + 1)/(sqrt u - 1) < sqrt 2, hence sqrt u > (sqrt2+1)/(sqrt2-1) = (sqrt2+1)^2 = 3+2*sqrt2 and u > (3+2*sqrt2)^2. This is a statement about tau_1 configurations ONLY; O.12 must cover every V, which is exactly the factor it gives up.
claims.notes: Elementary, and checked symbolically rather than by evaluating a float, because the threshold is exact and this repo has a recorded instance of a strict comparison at an exact boundary being decided by which algebraically equivalent expression was evaluated. PRIOR ART, stated because it was not checked first: the VALUES 13.9282 at X_1 = 1 and 33.9706 asymptotically were already in Note O, reached via |V| >= 2 from the parity lemma (which holds whenever M is odd). This claim does not discover them. What is new is the closed form (1+sqrt2)^4 = 17+12sqrt2, the family u > (sqrt2 V + sqrt(2V^2+1))^2 it sits in, and the characterisation of which V are admissible. Grepping for a number before deriving it costs one search and was not done.

claims.statement: The realised extremal windowed 4-cycles are the tau_1 ones, so O.13's threshold and not O.12's bound is what nature respects. At X = 6000 for D = 1 the twelve smallest unit-free cofactor ratios all have modulus ratio equal to tau_1^2 to five decimals, and the minimum 34.0811 at (37,1261) with moduli (866,1730) is 0.325% above (1+sqrt2)^4 = 33.970563. D = 2 likewise: minimum 34.0548 at (73,2486), 0.248% above. So O.12's proved 4.7913 is short by a factor 7.09 because it must allow non-tau_1 configurations (and, separately, because it carries the finite correction tau^2 < 3 rather than < 2). WITHDRAWN: an earlier version of this statement offered D = 4 as a converse -- its two sub-threshold cycles u = 19.2400 at (25,481) and 19.7267 at (35113,692665) being non-tau_1. That reading is wrong. At D = 4 the invariant is M*D, so the threshold is (u-1)*D/sqrt(u) > 2 sqrt2 V, i.e. u > 2+sqrt3 = 3.7321 at V = 2, and both values are ABOVE it: they are ordinary configurations, and the tau_1^2 they were compared against was the D = 1 formula. No converse is established, and the D-generalisation is not done.
claims.notes: Produced in the direction this note insists on -- enumerate realised configurations and read off which multiplier explains the ratio, occupancy as INPUT. Generating candidates from multipliers and testing occupancy afterwards is what produced every withdrawn r-product statistic in the O-thread. This converts the 7.11x looseness from an unexplained constant into an identified mechanism, which is the stronger form: 7.09x of it is the non-tau_1 allowance and 0.33% is how far the extremum sits above the tau_1 threshold. CAVEAT: this does NOT prove x^2+1 admits no non-tau_1 windowed 4-cycle. That is the cross-orbit case Note O repeatedly records as the one multipliers do not predict -- on (1, 115921) the multiplier product predicts a modulus ratio 1.31 against an observed minimum 33.77. Measured absence over a finite range, and a bound's silence is not evidence about what lies outside it. SELF-CORRECTION: the D = 4 converse was withdrawn before the follow-up commit, on checking the derivation against the M*D section rather than on anything failing. It had already shipped in 14109e1. Both a^2-ab+b^2 = 469^2 for (25,481) and the 0.632 ratio are correct arithmetic; what was wrong was reading them through the D = 1 multiplier equation. The correct V = 1 test at D = 4 is whether (M*D)^2 + ab is a square, and 3339001 is not. Pinned by a test so the reading cannot return.

claims.statement: The minimum unit-free cofactor ratio for x^2+1 is 34.0811 at (37, 1261) sharing moduli 866 and 1730, verified independently and unmoved at X = 3000 and 6000. All four products check: 37*866 = 179^2+1, 37*1730 = 253^2+1, 1261*866 = 1045^2+1, 1261*1730 = 1477^2+1. For x^2+1 the overall minimum is the same witness, so units do not enter -- unlike D = 2, where the overall minimum is 33.0000 at (1,33), the unit cofactor, against a unit-free 34.0548 at (73,2486). Against a dyadic band's 2, O.12 proves > 4.7913 (2.40x) where nature supplies >= 34.0811 (17.04x), so the theorem is loose by 7.11x with no sign of the bound being approached.
claims.notes: Found by the parallel session; verified here by an independent search over ratio_classes rather than by re-running theirs, at two sizes. ONE DETAIL WORTH ADDING: the extremal witness's MODULUS ratio is 1.99769 -- within 0.12% of the window's own bound of 2. So the configuration that is most extreme on the cofactor axis is nearly marginal on the modulus axis, which is the sort of thing that would matter if anyone tried to push the cofactor bound down by tightening the window. Recorded as a value, not a law: 34.0811 for D = 1 and 34.0548 for D = 2 agree to three figures and that is two points, on which this repo has a specific record of fitting laws it later withdrew.

claims.statement: Closing O.13's exceptional branch would improve O.12 from 4.7913 to 33.9706, a factor 7.09 and the largest improvement available to that theorem. Two congruence filters apply first: Eisenstein (a^2 - ab + b^2 a perfect square, for V = 1 to exist) and Gaussian (n | x^2+1 is solvable iff 4 does not divide n and n has no prime factor 3 mod 4, required of BOTH cofactors). Neither closes it. At a <= 1200 four primitive pairs pass both: (25,481) u = 19.2400, (505,7897) u = 15.6376, (865,22873) u = 26.4428, (985,29593) u = 30.0437. Walking x <= 3e6, none realises two shared moduli in one window -- and the reason is OCCUPANCY, not congruence: (25,481) does share two moduli, 2 and 53546 (25*2 = 7^2+1, 481*2 = 31^2+1), a ratio of 26773. So improving O.12 to O.13's threshold meets the same wall Note O records for O.2: any proof must be about occupancy, not congruences.
claims.notes: The Gaussian filter was the reason to hope: it is a condition on the cofactors that the Eisenstein one knows nothing about, so incompatibility was plausible. It is not incompatible, and the negative result is the useful one -- it says the 7.09x gap is not reachable by a sharper local argument. Bounded at a <= 1200 and x <= 3e6; larger a is untested and a bound's silence is not evidence about what lies outside it.

claims.statement: O.13' generalises to arbitrary D once every formula is taken in its M*D form: the conic is aY^2 - bX^2 = M*D, the multiplier equation U^2 - ab V^2 = (M*D)^2, and the window premise tau_V^2 < 2 + D/X_1^2. With s = V sqrt(ab)/(M*D) and c = 2 + D/X_1^2 a window needs s < (c-1)/(2 sqrt c), i.e. sqrt(u) - 1/sqrt(u) > 2 sqrt(c) V/((c-1) D); at D = 1 and X_1 -> infinity this recovers u > (1+sqrt2)^4. V = 2 is automatic for EVERY pair only at D = 1, where U = a+b gives (a+b)^2 - 4ab = M^2; for D != 1 it requires (M*D)^2 + 4ab to be a square, which holds for some pairs and not others, so the minimal admissible V is pair-dependent. Checked at X = 1500 against the smallest realised unit-free windowed 4-cycle for D = 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,11: NO violation at any D, and the bound is essentially attained at D = 1 (34.0811 against 33.9691, slack 1.00), D = 2 (34.2121 against 33.9556, 1.01) and D = 11 (1.3333 against 1.2348, 1.08), while loose at D = 4 (2.02) and D = 6 (2.94).
claims.notes: Closes the step O.13' recorded as not done. Its value is as much a POSITIVE CHECK on the corrected M*D forms as a result: three separate errors tonight came from using a D = 1 formula generally, and a machinery that produced no violation across nine D is evidence the corrected forms are right where re-reading them was not. Do not read the sharp cases as a pattern: D = 1, 2, 11 being near-tight while 4 and 6 are loose is nine points with no proposed mechanism, and this repo has a specific record of fitting laws to reproducible values. In particular D = 11 being both the first failing D and near-tight is exactly the kind of near-miss that has been refuted here before.

claims.statement: The anchored-window defect has been swept for across the whole repo and is closed. Six experiments step a band multiplicatively -- exp01 (D *= 2), exp09 (M *= 2), exp15 (M *= 4), exp16 (M *= 2), exp20 (N *= 4), exp24 (N *= 2) -- but anchoring is a defect only where the CLAIM quantifies over every band while the sweep visits anchored ones. Checking each claim's wording against its experiment: exp01 and exp15 are cited by no claim; exp16's seven claims are fits and samplings, with the one universal phrase ('almost every modulus carries a single x') being an asymptotic statement rather than a sweep quantifier; exp24's fourteen include three with universal wording, and all three rest on O.12's PROOF rather than on the sweep. The two genuine cases were exp09's degree ladder and exp20's mean-G decay, both found and both fixed.
claims.notes: The detector was validated before its clean result was believed, per the rule that a clean audit is broken until it has failed on a known case. Run against the registry as it stood four commits ago it flags BOTH pre-fix claims -- the granularity claim's 'over pairs in a dyadic band [N,2N)' and rational-gram-bounded-on-windows' 'on every dyadic window [M,2M)' -- so its silence on the rest is informative. THE AUDIT'S OWN LIMIT, stated because three audits tonight had the defect they hunted: it matches English quantifiers, so a claim that quantifies universally without the words 'every/all/each/any' would pass unseen. What it cannot do is distinguish a universal claim backed by a proof from one backed by a sweep -- that judgement was made by reading each of the three.

claims.statement: The doubly-banded reading of Ford-Maynard's Type II configuration is VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not inferred, on three independent grounds. (1) THE SHARED VARIABLE IS WINDOW-CONFINED BY THEIR OWN DEFINITION OF J. p. 7: 'J subset (x/2, x] containing x^{1-c} elements'. Footnote 2 counts #{n : n m1, n m2 in J}; n m1 in J forces x/2 < n m1 <= x, i.e. x/(2 m1) < n <= x/m1, a ratio of EXACTLY 2. Every n counted lies in one dyadic window for free -- the window is not a restriction this repo imposes, it is forced by J sitting inside a dyadic interval. (2) THE PAIR IS BANDED BY THE FOOTNOTE'S OWN NOTATION: 'on average over m1, m2 ~ x^{1-2c+eps}'. So the footnote quantity is doubly banded, which is exactly Theorem O.12's configuration. (3) AND (II) ITSELF IMPLIES EVERY DOUBLY-BANDED RESTRICTION. (II) is stated 'For any complex numbers xi_m, kappa_n with |xi_m| <= tau^B(m) and |kappa_n| <= tau^B(n)' (p. 2), so taking xi_m = 0 off [M,2M) and kappa_n = 0 off [N,2N) -- both admissible, since 0 and 1 are at most tau^B -- gives the same bound on any pair of dyadic sub-bands. Its n is confined in any case, since the sum carries x/2 < mn <= x. Note that (II)'s m-range ((x/2)^theta, x^{theta+nu}] is NOT itself a band when nu > 0; it is route (3), the arbitrariness of the coefficients, that supplies the banding there.
claims.citation: Ford-Maynard, arXiv:2407.14368v1, p. 2 for (II) and its coefficient quantifier; p. 7 for J subset (x/2,x] and for footnote 2.
claims.notes: Settles the residual that CLAUDE.md identified as what gaussian-to-rational-bridge actually carries -- 'the reading of what (II) quantifies over ... which COULD be settled by reading more carefully'. It could, and this is that reading. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: the step from 'the count is 0/1' to 'nu = 0 in their sense' rests on the footnote's own four-word hedge, 'closely related to'. That is the source's hedge, not this repo's, and it is off the path: nu = 0 comes from selberg-nu-zero-binds, which is quoted with an empty depends_on. So the footnote is corroboration that we measure the object the literature names as the barrier, not a derivation step. Found by going to the paper for a question the notes had marked as answerable by going to the paper -- the flag was two months old and correct.
